title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Share DIV and REM through a fused-subtract unsigned divider
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12, median Fmax
5.442 MHz, and a 199.837 ns worst path spanning forwarding and the EX ALU
with 156 cells. There are no prior divider experiments or LESSONS.md.
alu.sv independently expresses signed and unsigned division and remainder
with / and %, leaving arithmetic sharing and divider topology to Gowin.
Their deep combinational logic is the strongest RTL-level explanation for
this path, though the available path summary does not identify an operator.
A smaller, explicitly shared divider with one subtract/borrow decision per
quotient bit can improve the clock period without costing CoreMark cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath with one combinational
unsigned restoring divider that produces both quotient and remainder.
For DIV and REM, convert operands to unsigned two's-complement magnitudes;
for DIVU and REMU, use the original unsigned operands. Restore the quotient
sign from a[31] XOR b[31], and the remainder sign from a[31], only for the
signed operations. Select quotient versus remainder after the shared core.

Implement the divider as 32 statically unrolled, progressively sized stages.
Starting with R_0 = 0, stage k = 1..32 forms the k-bit trial remainder
T_k = {R_(k-1), magnitude_a[32-k]}. Compute a single (k+1)-bit unsigned
difference D_k = {1'b0, T_k} - {1'b0, magnitude_b[k-1:0]}. Accept it only
when all divisor bits above k-1 are zero and D_k[k] is zero. The accepted
decision is quotient[32-k]; R_k is D_k[k-1:0] if accepted, otherwise T_k.
At k=32 the upper-divisor-zero condition is constant true. Use static
generate widths, with an explicit first stage, and share the upper-bit
nonzero reductions. Derive the comparison directly from the subtraction's
borrow bit; do not infer a separate comparator followed by a subtractor.
This keeps early stages narrow and makes quotient/remainder sharing explicit.

Handle divisor zero with the required all-ones quotient and original-dividend
remainder, bypassing signed quotient correction for that case. Preserve
INT_MIN / -1 = INT_MIN and INT_MIN % -1 = 0, including the unsigned
magnitude 0x80000000. Keep the RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS expressions bit-for-bit
unchanged and exclude the real divider from that branch. Preserve the ALU
interface, all other operations, nret=1, pipeline registers, bus handshakes,
forwarding, decoder legality, retirement ordering, and existing checks.
This is a local combinational arithmetic optimization with zero added cycles.

Validate real arithmetic with the existing ALU suite plus deterministic
signed/unsigned quotient-remainder edge and randomized vectors; run the
normal formal and cosim gates and canonical CoreMark CRC validation. Measure
the resulting divider path and median Fmax with the Gowin flow. CoreMark
marker-delimited cycles should be unchanged; a clock gain exceeding 4.6%
is required for acceptance. The main risk is that Gowin already shares some
operators, or that magnitude conversion and sign correction offset the
reduction in divider logic and routing. The proposed gain is unmeasured.

title: Move DIV/REM into a shared iterative execution unit
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: 12.12 CoreMark iterations/s,
5.442 MHz median Fmax, and 12,312 LUT4s. Its worst path takes 199.837 ns
through forwarding and the execute ALU, with 156 cells. The ALU implements
signed and unsigned division and remainder as combinational / and %.
These operators are a strong explanation for the deep arithmetic path:
even instructions that do not divide pay its clock-period cost. There is
no LESSONS.md and no prior structural attempt in the available log.

The only recorded experiment is the baseline: 12.12 CoreMark iterations/s,
5.442 MHz median Fmax, and 12,312 LUT4s. Its worst path takes 199.837 ns

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the combinational DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU circuits with one shared,
bounded-latency iterative divider inside alu.sv. Keep integer operations
and multiplication on their existing execution paths. This is one
structural change: separate variable-latency division from ordinary EX.

Use unsigned restoring division with four quotient bits computed per
cycle by four explicitly bounded shift/subtract/select steps, for eight
iteration cycles. Register the normalized operands and signedness at
request acceptance, retain the original dividend, and keep quotient and
remainder state in the unit. Use explicitly widened trial subtraction
to avoid losing the carry/borrow. Quotient sign is the operand-sign XOR;
remainder sign follows the dividend. Preserve divide-by-zero results
(all-ones quotient and original dividend remainder) and INT_MIN/-1
results (INT_MIN quotient, zero remainder). Remove all real / and %
hardware from the instantiated combinational ALU path.

Add request and completion handshakes. Latch post-forwarding operands
exactly once, including their RVFI source values. Hold PC and ID/EX while
a division is outstanding, but let older EX/MEM and MEM/WB instructions
drain. Once the older EX/MEM instruction advances, inject an EX/MEM
bubble with side-effect controls cleared on every divider-wait cycle;
holding that older entry would replay stores or retirement. Existing
dmem backpressure must still hold an unaccepted older memory request.
Preserve a completed result until EX/MEM accepts it, transfer the divide
exactly once, then resume ordinary forwarding and issue. Do not restart
the held divide, forward its partial quotient, or lose operands when
older forwarding sources drain. Reset cancels pending work.

Expose the final iteration's corrected result for EX/MEM acceptance on
that same edge when downstream is ready; otherwise save it in a sticky
completion register. Avoid an unnecessary extra completion cycle. Check
that even branch-to-divide and consecutive-divide instruction streams
meet the existing ten-cycle formal liveness observation interval under
the formal wrapper's ready-bus assumptions. Keep the formal configs
untouched. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, use the existing exact XOR formulas
with the same request, wait, completion and consumption control, so
formal still exercises the multicycle integration rather than bypassing
its hazards. Keep multiplication's real and ALTOPS behavior unchanged.

The expected gain comes from replacing roughly a full divide's serial
arithmetic with four subtract/select steps per iteration and sharing
quotient/remainder hardware. Extra division cycles may reduce CoreMark
iterations/cycle; the prediction is that Fmax improvement dominates.
The multiplier, forwarding or register-file path may become the next
bottleneck. Validate the actual tradeoff with the unchanged stall-driven
CoreMark CRC/marker checks and median Gowin Fmax; require fitness above
12.67752 to clear the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold. Preserve nret=1,
the core port contract, trap behavior, and every existing invariant.

title: Early direct-branch prediction with a 64-entry bimodal table
motivation:
The baseline always fetches PC+4 and flushes on every taken branch or
jump. IF/ID is combinational, so each such redirect loses one potential
instruction-acceptance cycle, not the two-cycle penalty suggested by
the five-stage description. CoreMark's repeated loops and direct calls
should benefit from predicting their successors before EX. The recorded
199.837 ns critical path runs through forwarding and the combinational
ALU, leaving substantial apparent timing headroom for a small predictor;
this proposal targets iterations/cycle rather than claiming a divider
timing improvement. LESSONS.md is absent and log.jsonl contains only the
baseline, with no previous predictor experiments.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one early direct-control-flow predictor: a 64-entry, two-bit
saturating direction table indexed by fetch PC[7:2], together with
combinational B/J immediate extraction and a shared PC-relative target
adder. Reset counters to weakly taken (2'b10). Predict legal conditional
branches from the counter MSB and legal JAL instructions unconditionally
taken; predict all other instructions, including JALR, sequentially.
Only predict an aligned direct target; leave the existing EX misalignment
trap behavior intact. This has 128 bits of learned state and needs no
BTB, tags, return stack, global history, or additional pipeline stage.

Carry the exact predicted next PC with each accepted instruction through
IF/ID and ID/EX. In EX compute the actual successor using the existing
forwarded branch comparison, JAL/JALR target calculation, and trap
fallback to PC+4. Redirect and squash the younger instruction only when
that successor differs from the saved prediction. Use the resolved
successor for EX/MEM.pc_next and RVFI regardless of prediction. Correct
predictions must neither flush nor insert a bubble, and a predicted-taken
branch that resolves not-taken must recover to its own PC+4.

Prediction takes effect only on an accepted instruction: imem is ready,
there is no load-use or data-memory hold, and no older EX recovery is
squashing the fetch. Hold both instruction and prediction metadata across
data stalls and clear both on bubbles. Train exactly once when a valid,
legal conditional branch advances from EX, excluding a misalignment trap;
saturate its PC-indexed counter toward its resolved direction. A held EX
branch must not repeatedly train. Read the pre-edge counter value on a
simultaneous same-index read/write and save the prediction actually used.

Gate EX recovery and training with valid and !stall_ex_mem. During a
data-memory hold, keep the PC and ID/EX state stable and defer recovery
until EX can advance. On release, recovery overrides instruction-memory
backpressure and any younger load-use hold, flushes the younger payload,
and installs the actual successor. Preserve the existing retained WB
forwarding values during data stalls. Derive prediction from raw fetch
data and PC, independently of flush-substituted NOPs; do not create a
combinational prediction/flush/hazard feedback loop. Table aliasing may
affect accuracy only, never architectural state or retirement order.

The expected gain is roughly 10 percent in fitness from fewer control
bubbles at approximately unchanged Fmax; this is a hypothesis, not a
measured result. Key risks are table aliasing, instruction stalls hiding
baseline redirect bubbles, and placement disruption from added logic.
Validate with the unchanged formal and cosimulation gates, canonical
CoreMark CRCs and marker timing under both bus-stall streams, and median
Gowin Fmax times iterations/cycle. Acceptance requires greater than 4.6
percent fitness improvement, not merely a lower cycle count. Preserve
nret=1, decoder legality, M-extension hardware and ALTOPS semantics, all
memory-side interfaces, and every existing verification invariant.

title: Halve serial divider depth with parallel radix-4 digit selection
motivation:
The champion reaches 91.82 iterations/s at 41.241 MHz, but its reported
worst path still starts at cpu/u_ex/u_alu/remainder_q_5_s0 and passes
through the divider and EX to data memory: 29.998 ns and 131 cells.
Each iteration currently chains four restoring subtract/select steps,
followed on completion by sign correction and the EX result mux.
LESSONS.md establishes division depth as the dominant clock bottleneck.
The prior micro_opt attempt, hyp-20261002-001-r1s0, reduced area but
regressed to 3.887 MHz by retaining a full combinational divider.
Optimize the champion's bounded iteration datapath instead: reducing
its serial arithmetic depth can improve every instruction's clock rate
without increasing division stalls or changing pipeline control.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real iterative divider's four serial radix-2 steps
with two serial radix-4 steps. Each radix-4 step produces two quotient
bits by evaluating subtraction candidates concurrently. Retain exactly
four quotient bits per iteration, eight iteration cycles per request,
and the existing request, final-iteration bypass, and sticky completion
protocol. This is a local arithmetic implementation change inside
alu.sv, with no new pipeline stage or execution scheduling policy.

On request acceptance, form the existing unsigned divisor magnitude D
and register D and 3*D. Form 2*D by wiring a left shift of registered D.
Represent all multiples as unsigned 34-bit values: 3*(2^32-1) must not
wrap. Compute 3*D as the explicitly widened sum of D and 2*D on the
request path, never by an adder in the iteration feedback path. Retain
the existing captured dividend, quotient magnitude, sign flags, and
divide-by-zero flag. Reset the added state with the existing divider.

For each of two statically generated digit steps, let R be the current
32-bit remainder and Q the 32-bit combined dividend/quotient shift
register. Form the unsigned 34-bit trial T = {R, Q[31:30]}. In parallel
compute three 35-bit differences Xk = {1'b0,T} - {1'b0,k*D}, for
k = 1, 2, 3. Let gk = !Xk[34], using the subtraction's borrow bit
directly rather than a separate comparison followed by subtraction.
Select the largest k whose difference is nonnegative, or zero if none
qualifies. With positive D the g bits are monotonic, so implement the
mutually exclusive selects s0=!g1, s1=g1&&!g2, s2=g2&&!g3, s3=g3.
Use masked candidate data and a balanced OR for the remainder selection
to avoid a cascaded priority mux. The two quotient bits are
{g2, g3 || (g1 && !g2)}. The next Q is {Q[29:0], digit}; the next R
selects T[31:0], X1[31:0], X2[31:0], or X3[31:0] with s0..s3.
Feed that R and Q into the second identical step, then into the same
iteration registers and final-result logic used by the current unit.

For D != 0, R < D implies T < 4*D; thus the selected digit is in 0..3
and the selected remainder is below D and fits 32 bits. Keep all 34
trial and divisor-multiple bits through the borrow decision; truncate
only the selected remainder. Preserve the explicit zero-divisor result
override, signed quotient correction, dividend-signed remainder, and
INT_MIN/-1 behavior. Keep the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arithmetic and
its identical eight-iteration protocol; the new candidate-subtraction
hardware belongs only in the real-arithmetic branch. Keep the ALU's
other operations, EX integration, bus behavior, nret=1, decoder checks,
and every architectural and verification invariant unchanged.

This trades four serial subtract/select stages for two stages, each
containing three parallel subtractors. The extra subtractors, D3
register, candidate routing, and selection fanout cost area, but the
champion uses only 2806 LUT4s. The main risks are Gowin implementing
the selection as a slow priority network, the request-time D3 adder
becoming critical, or multiplication/sign correction becoming the
next clock limit. Expected fitness improvement is 20 percent, an
unmeasured prediction, with unchanged marker-delimited CoreMark cycles.
Use median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle to judge success;
require fitness above 96.04372 to clear the champion by more than 4.6
percent. Do not change iteration count to obtain the timing gain.

Validate real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU with all existing arithmetic and protocol
tests plus digit-threshold and wide-multiple cases. Check direct final
iteration acceptance, prolonged result backpressure, changing live
operands after launch, reset cancellation, and consecutive requests.
Run the unchanged formal and cosim gates and canonical CoreMark CRC,
UART, and marker checks under the existing instruction/data stalls.
ALTOPS formal alone is insufficient to validate the new arithmetic;
retain real-arithmetic unit coverage and the unchanged formal-deep
obligation. Measure the actual path and area with the vendor flow.

title: Retime division with a launch-time prefix and registered completion boundary
motivation:
The structural attempt hyp-20261002-002-r1s1 raised fitness to 91.82
and median Gowin Fmax to 41.241 MHz by making division iterative.
LESSONS.md and log.jsonl show that arithmetic sharing without registers
failed, while prediction left the original divider timing bottleneck.
The champion's recorded 29.998 ns worst path starts at
cpu/u_ex/u_alu/remainder_q_5_s0 and passes through the ALU and EX toward
dmem. In the current RTL, last_iteration exposes four serial restoring
steps, result selection and sign correction directly to EX/MEM.
This is evidence for retiming the divider's completion path; it is not
evidence that another instruction pipeline stage or a predictor is needed.

hypothesis.motivation:
The structural attempt hyp-20261002-002-r1s1 raised fitness to 91.82
and median Gowin Fmax to 41.241 MHz by making division iterative.
LESSONS.md and log.jsonl show that arithmetic sharing without registers
failed, while prediction left the original divider timing bottleneck.
The champion's recorded 29.998 ns worst path starts at
cpu/u_ex/u_alu/remainder_q_5_s0 and passes through the ALU and EX toward
dmem. In the current RTL, last_iteration exposes four serial restoring

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Redistribute the existing division work across request capture, seven
full-width iteration cycles, and a completion phase. Compute the first
four quotient bits during request acceptance, where the partial dividend
is only the leading four bits of the normalized dividend. After the
remaining seven four-bit iterations, expose only registered quotient
and remainder state to sign correction and EX. This is one structural
retiming of the divider, with the same externally visible latency and
request/result interface as the champion.

Let A and D be the unsigned operand magnitudes already required for
signed DIV/REM, and the original operands for unsigned operations. On
request acceptance, divide the four-bit prefix A[31:28] by D to obtain
a four-bit prefix quotient q4 and prefix remainder r4. For D >= 16,
q4 is zero and r4 is A[31:28]. For nonzero D < 16, use four explicitly
narrow restoring steps on D[3:0], with five-bit trial subtraction so
borrow is retained. Qualify this small network with D[31:4] == 0;
never truncate a large divisor into the small-divisor case. The D == 0
path may initialize q4 to zero and r4 to the prefix because final
zero-divisor override supplies the architectural answer. Avoid full-width
division operators or four full-width steps in the request path.

Capture quotient_q = {A[27:0], q4}, remainder_q = {28'b0, r4}, and
divisor_q = D on that same acceptance edge. Capture original dividend,
signedness, result selection, and forwarded RVFI operands exactly once
as today. Perform seven subsequent iterations of the existing four
widened shift/subtract/select steps, preserving their borrow discipline.
At the seventh iteration edge the entire unsigned quotient and remainder
are registered; freeze these states and enter sticky completion.

Remove the last_iteration-to-final_result arithmetic bypass. During
completion, select quotient_q or remainder_q and apply the saved sign
and zero-divisor override directly from these stable registers. No
quotient_step[4] or remainder_step[4] signal may feed div_result. Keep
div_result_valid asserted and these sources unchanged until the result
handshake. An additional corrected-result register must not add a cycle.
With request accepted at edge t0, compute the remaining 28 bits at
edges t1 through t7; valid rises after t7 and EX/MEM can accept at t8.
This matches the current final-iteration bypass's earliest consumption
at t8, including consecutive divisions and branch-to-divide streams.

Preserve exact DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU results, particularly zero divisors,
negative remainders, INT_MIN operands and INT_MIN/-1. Under
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, retain each exact XOR formula and use the same
seven-iteration/completion control and visible handshake timing as the
real unit. Keep the existing single-outstanding execution protocol:
older instructions drain, a stalled older memory request remains held,
divider waits insert side-effect-free EX/MEM bubbles, and the result
transfers exactly once. Reset cancels both active and completed work.
Preserve nret=1, core ports, decoder/trap rules and all existing checks.

The expected improvement is about 20 percent in fitness, principally
from Fmax with unchanged marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. The internal
four-step recurrence remains, but its path ends at divider state rather
than continuing through sign correction and EX result selection.
An independent Python model of the proposed prefix initialization and
seven iterations matched integer reference results on 119492 signed,
unsigned, quotient and remainder cases, including corner cases and
random operands. This checks the arithmetic proposal, not RTL or timing.
The prefix logic is narrow; nevertheless magnitude normalization followed
by prefix selection could become critical, or another existing path
could cap the gain. This prediction is unmeasured. Run the arithmetic,
pipeline, formal and cosimulation gates, including the unchanged formal
liveness window, then compare canonical stalled CoreMark cycles/CRCs
and median Gowin Fmax. Acceptance requires fitness above 96.04372,
more than 4.6 percent above 91.82; do not change the evaluation contract.

title: Compact early branch prediction on the iterative-divider champion
motivation:
The current champion still fetches sequentially and flushes on every
taken branch or jump. Its IF/ID bundle is combinational, so an EX
redirect wastes one instruction-acceptance opportunity. LESSONS.md and
log.jsonl report that hyp-20261002-003-r1s2's 64-entry bimodal predictor
with early JAL reduced stalled CoreMark cycles from 4491485 to 4201709,
a 6.45 percent reduction, and passed formal and cosimulation. That
candidate lost to the iterative-divider champion because it retained
combinational division, not because prediction increased cycle count.
Apply this demonstrated predictor mechanism to the supplied champion,
preserving its shared eight-cycle divider and existing execute holds.
Both the baseline and current champion logged 4491485 measured cycles,
making the earlier predictor result a useful, though unproven, estimate.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 64-entry, two-bit saturating direction table indexed by fetch
PC[7:2], reset to weakly taken (2'b10). In the existing combinational
fetch/decode stage, recognize only legal conditional-branch encodings
and JAL, extract the B/J immediate, and form PC plus the immediate with
a shared direct-target adder. Predict a conditional branch taken from
its counter MSB and JAL taken unconditionally, only for word-aligned
targets. All other instructions, including JALR and reserved branch
encodings, predict PC+4. This is one early direct-control-flow predictor;
it needs no BTB, return stack, global history, or new pipeline stage.

Carry one predicted_taken bit with each accepted instruction through
if_id_t and id_ex_t. A full predicted-next-PC register and 32-bit EX
equality comparator are unnecessary here: every predicted target is
computed from that same instruction's PC and immediate, never from a
cached target. EX independently recomputes the target and resolves the
branch using the existing forwarded operands. For direct branches and
JAL, recover when predicted_taken differs from the resolved transfer
decision after the existing misalignment suppression. JALR remains
unpredicted and redirects on each valid aligned execution. A direction
mismatch with a target equal to PC+4 may harmlessly recover to PC+4.
Recovery uses the actual target when effectively taken, otherwise the
instruction's own PC+4. Correct predictions must not flush or bubble.
EX/MEM.pc_next and RVFI always describe the resolved architectural
successor; jump links and all trap behavior retain their current rules.

Derive prediction from the registered fetch PC and raw imem_data,
independently of flush-substituted NOPs and hazard outputs. Apply the
predicted successor only when the current fetch is accepted: imemReady
is high, there is no load-use, dmem, or execute_wait hold, and no older
recovery squashes the instruction. Capture the exact prediction used
on that edge with its instruction. Hold metadata through stalls and
clear it on reset or bubbles. Predictor training may change a stalled
fetch's combinational prediction, but neither its PC nor its ID/EX
metadata may advance until acceptance. Do not create combinational
prediction/flush/hazard feedback paths.

Define EX advancement as valid and not stalled by older data memory
and not execute_wait, qualified against reset. Train exactly once on
each advancing legal conditional branch without a misalignment trap,
saturating the counter selected by that branch's own PC toward its
actual direction. Use the current table value for each update, and
pre-edge table contents for a simultaneous fetch lookup; no update-to-
lookup combinational bypass is needed. Aliasing affects accuracy only.
Qualify recovery with the same advancement event. In particular, a
branch held behind an older stalled memory operation must neither
repeatedly train nor redirect. On release, recovery overrides imem
backpressure, installs the resolved successor and squashes the younger
fetch. Keep existing retained-WB forwarding and DIV/REM request,
operand capture, completion and hold semantics intact. Recovery and
training must not form a feedback loop through execute_wait.

Reproducing the earlier cycle reduction at 41.241 MHz would yield
approximately 98.15 CoreMark iterations/second, about 6.9 percent above
91.82. The greater-than-4.6-percent acceptance threshold is about 96.04;
at 4201709 cycles the design needs roughly 40.36 MHz, allowing only a
2.1 percent Fmax loss. Thus the hypothesis is a 7 percent fitness gain
with medium confidence, not a measured result. The compact metadata
and direction-only recovery reduce predictor costs, but the new
instruction-memory-to-PC target-adder path, table read mux, and Gowin
placement changes could still erase the gain. Use the unchanged formal
and cosimulation gates, canonical 2K CoreMark CRCs/UART and marker
timing with both bus-stall streams, and median Gowin Fmax multiplied
by measured iterations/cycle to judge the result. Preserve nret=1,
decoder legality, all memory/RVFI interfaces and every hard invariant.

title: Remove redirect feedback through instruction masking and load-use decode
motivation:
The champion scores 102.63 at median Gowin Fmax 46.095 MHz. Its reported
worst path starts at cpu/u_ex/reg_q.rd_1_s0 and ends at an ID/EX rs2_val
register, traversing forwarding, EX, IF, hazard logic, and ID: 28.258 ns
arrival and 55 cells. The previous micro_opt radix-4 divider attempt,
hyp-20261002-001-r2s0, exposed the same control-path family at 45.934 MHz.
LESSONS.md shows that the successful registered divider completion moved
the bottleneck, while branch prediction lost enough Fmax to erase its
cycle savings. In the current RTL, redirect forces a NOP onto the whole
IF instruction bus before register-file addressing, decode, and load-use
comparison. A late forwarded branch decision therefore propagates back
through work whose result will be discarded. Remove this combinational
dependency rather than changing branch prediction or divider arithmetic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make instruction annulment a local ID register/control operation instead
of a redirect-controlled transformation of the incoming instruction bits.
This is one combinational control-cone optimization: retain the existing
pipeline registers, taken-branch penalty, PC redirect priority, and every
divide and memory handshake.

In if_stage, drive out.instr directly from imem_data, independent of
flush and redirect. Keep out.pc, PC advancement, reset, redirect-over-stall
priority, and out.valid = !(flush || redirect) as today. The raw instruction
fields reaching the register file, decoder, immediate generator, and
hazard comparisons must no longer depend on the EX redirect signal.

In hazard_unit, qualify the existing raw-field load-use predicate with
imem_ready, because instruction data is not usable when that bus stalls.
Use imem_ready && id_ex_mem_read && id_ex_rd != 0 &&
(id_ex_rd == if_id_rs1 || id_ex_rd == if_id_rs2). Do not qualify this
predicate with redirect, flush_if, or if_id.valid: those would recreate
the late redirect feedback. Preserve the current stall/flush equations,
older-data-memory hold priority, execute_wait handling, and direct
redirect-to-flush_id path. A legal instruction in EX cannot simultaneously
be a load and a branch/jump, so raw wrong-path operand fields cannot
create an architectural load-use hold on a redirect. Keep the existing
conservative comparisons for instructions without real rs operands;
eliminating false source dependencies is outside this hypothesis.

In id_stage, keep reset/flush clearing the register and keep stall holding
its entire existing entry. Only when !stall captures an incoming entry,
latch ctrl_decoded if in.valid, otherwise latch an all-zero ctrl_t with
valid cleared. In particular clear mem_read, mem_write, reg_write,
is_branch, and is_jump for an invalid fetch even when its raw bits encode
a store or jump. Data and RVFI payload fields may capture the ordinary
raw decoded values on this invalid entry; they cannot produce effects.
Do not put !in.valid into an unconditional reset/flush condition, which
would destroy a held real instruction during dmem or divider stalls.
Existing reset/flush behavior may continue to zero the complete bundle.
The valid decoder still defaults to illegal and validates encodings
exactly as before; clearing bubble controls does not make a retiring
illegal instruction legal. EX currently relies on neutral bubble controls
for redirect and memory suppression, so clearing valid alone is unsafe.

The intended timing change is to remove redirect from the instruction
mux, register-file read-address cone, and load-use equality cone. Redirect
still directly annuls ID/EX and updates PC, but should no longer traverse
those decode/read cones before reaching their register inputs or enables.
No architectural cycles should change, including with the existing
approximately 22 percent instruction/data stalls. The expected fitness
gain is 12 percent through Fmax, an unmeasured estimate. Another path,
including the divider recurrence or direct branch-to-PC path, may cap
the gain; added control gating must remain at the ID register boundary.

Preserve nret=1 and all top-level ports, RVFI ordering and operands,
exception rules, M-extension real and ALTOPS behavior, and every existing
check. Validate invalid fetches carrying real store/jump/illegal bits,
load-use interlocks, forwarded branches/JALR, redirects overlapping either
bus stall, and unavailable fetches during divider holds. An exhaustive
Python check of the old and proposed load-use/control equations matched
on 1310720 combinations of source/destination indices and control bits,
assuming the decoder constraint that loads and divide waits cannot
redirect. This checks the control proposal, not RTL or timing.
Run existing formal, cocotb,
and cosimulation gates and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks.
Compare marker-delimited cycles and median vendor Fmax with the champion;
acceptance requires fitness strictly above 107.35098, more than 4.6
percent above 102.63. No timing or performance gain is claimed measured.

title: Separate pipeline validity from fetch data to cut redirect feedback
motivation:
The champion scores 102.63 at 46.095 MHz after divider retiming. Its
reported worst path now starts at EX/MEM rd, traverses forwarding,
EX branch resolution, IF, hazard control and ID, and takes 28.258 ns
through 55 cells. The other round-two divider attempt exposed the
same module chain. In the current frontend, redirect selects a NOP
onto the whole instruction before decode, register-file addressing,
and load-use comparison; ID then clears its entire payload on flush.
This couples late branch resolution to data preparation for an
instruction that will be discarded. LESSONS.md and the structural
entries in log.jsonl establish that divider isolation already helped;
the next evidence-supported target is this frontend control topology.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace instruction-as-NOP bubble transport with explicit stage
validity and local side-effect qualification. This is one structural
reorganization of the pipeline's squash and interlock network, with
no extra stage, prediction mechanism, or instruction latency. Keep
the existing divider and integer/multiply datapaths unchanged.

Drive IF's instruction payload directly from imem_data even when the
fetch will be discarded. Fetch availability comes from imemReady;
redirect must not select instruction bits or register-file addresses.
Decode and register-file reads may compute arbitrary results for an
unavailable or wrong-path fetch. Qualify load-use interlocking with
the valid EX load and available fetch, comparing the raw source fields
without routing them through a redirect-controlled NOP mux. Retain
the current conservative source-field comparison to keep this change
focused; source-use optimization is outside the proposal.

Separate ID/EX payload updates from its valid-bit updates. Reset may
still initialize the payload, but squash must only annul validity,
not zero every data/control bit. With older dmem backpressure or an
outstanding divide, retain the current instruction and payload. When
those holds release, a redirect or load-use bubble clears ID/EX.valid;
otherwise a newly available fetch supplies validity. The payload may
load decoded raw instruction data when not locally held, including on
a redirect cycle. Its enable must not acquire a redirect dependence.
A branch redirect still overrides the PC hold and annuls the next
instruction on the same cycle as today. Preserve repeated redirects
while a branch is held behind an older stalled memory operation.
Concretely, let backend_hold = dmem_stall || execute_wait and let
load_use use valid-qualified raw source comparisons. The payload
enable is !backend_hold && !load_use. The next ID/EX valid bit holds
under backend_hold, clears on redirect || load_use otherwise, and
takes imemReady otherwise. Thus redirect reaches the valid register
but not the payload enable or the raw load-use comparison.

Explicit validity is the sole authority for executing instructions.
Qualify EX branch/jump redirects, divider launches, producer tags,
hazard detection, memory reads/writes and retirement with the relevant
stage validity. Invalid decoded controls must never launch division,
redirect, interlock as a load, forward a false result, access memory,
or write a register. Keep invalid payload values as don't-care data;
avoid recreating a wide squash mux downstream. On divider-wait cycles,
older stages still drain and EX/MEM becomes invalid unless held by an
unaccepted memory request. Preserve all trap and alignment behavior
for valid instructions, and discard wrong-path illegal instructions.

Preserve the existing retained-WB forwarding exception deliberately:
MEM/WB.valid clears during dmem stalls, but its already-written value
can still be needed by the held EX instruction. Use a separate bypass
producer-valid bit/tag that is retained with the MEM/WB payload on
these stalls, loaded from the incoming valid producer on a normal
transfer, and cleared when a bubble replaces that payload. Do not
simply gate WB forwarding with retirement valid. EX/MEM forwarding
uses a valid producer and keeps the existing younger-writer priority;
x0 never forwards. Register-file writes and RVFI retirement continue
to use retirement validity, not bypass availability.

The expected improvement is 15 percent in fitness, principally from
shortening the redirect-to-ID path while retaining CoreMark cycles.
This is an unmeasured prediction. Redirect still reaches the PC and

title: Early branch prediction with recovery isolated from decode data
motivation:
The two previous predictor attempts reduced marker-delimited stalled
CoreMark cycles from 4491485 to 4201709, a 6.45 percent saving. However,
hyp-20261002-003-r2s2 lost 7.1 percent Fmax and regressed in fitness.
Simply repeating that integration is not enough. The current champion
has since registered divider completion and reaches 46.095 MHz, with
its reported worst path traversing forwarding, EX, IF, hazard logic
and ID. The source explains this path: EX redirect masks all fetch
instruction bits to a NOP before register-file addressing, immediate
extraction, decoding and load-use detection. This late recovery signal
needlessly enters the younger instruction's data path. A direct-branch
predictor whose recovery only kills pipeline controls can retain the
demonstrated cycle saving while shortening this particular timing path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one early direct-control-flow predictor with recovery isolated
from decode data. Retain the previously demonstrated 64-entry two-bit
bimodal direction table indexed by fetch PC[7:2], initially weakly taken
(2'b10), and unconditional early JAL prediction. Recognize legal BRANCH
funct3 values and JAL from raw imem_data, extract their B/J immediate,
and share a PC-relative target adder. Predict only word-aligned targets;
JALR and every other instruction predict PC+4. Add no BTB, return stack,
history register or pipeline stage. The new architectural emphasis is
integrating recovery at the register control boundary instead of
feeding a late EX decision back through the entire decode data cone.

Pass raw imem_data through IF to the decoder, immediate generator,
register-file read addresses and load-use address comparisons without
any redirect/flush-to-NOP mux. Keep fetch availability as a separate
control signal. Decode and operand data may be meaningless on a killed
cycle; they must never acquire valid side-effect controls. In ID/EX,
separate payload updates from validity/control updates. Recovery must
not gate, clear or select PC, instruction, immediate, source addresses,
destination address or operand-data registers on non-reset cycles.
Those payload flops can capture raw decode data when normally enabled,
even on a killed cycle. Reset may retain the existing full initialization.
On a bubble, explicitly clear valid, the entire ctrl bundle, and the
prediction bit. Merely clearing valid is UNSAFE in this core because
memory enables and forwarding eligibility currently use ctrl fields
without uniformly checking valid. Preserve that existing downstream
discipline by always giving invalid entries zero side-effect controls.

Preserve the existing load-use comparison policy, but evaluate it from
raw source bits and qualify a useful dependency with imem readiness and
a valid load in EX, independently of recovery. A raw wrong-path source
match must never suppress correction: recovery has priority over a
younger load-use hold and over imem backpressure. An older data-memory
stall or a divider execution hold still holds ID/EX and the PC. Define
EX advancement from valid, !reset, !stall_ex_mem and !execute_wait;
recovery and predictor training occur only on this event. Thus a branch
behind an older blocked memory operation defers recovery until release.
On that release, recovery sets the PC to the resolved successor and
injects a zero-control ID/EX bubble regardless of imem readiness. With
no hard hold, imem not ready also injects a zero-control bubble while
holding the PC; it must not decode unavailable raw data into live control.
Implement these priorities explicitly without a combinational path
from recovery through fetch data, source-address comparators, decode,
or the register-file read muxes. Retain the existing WB data preservation
during dmem stalls and all divider request/completion behavior.

Carry exactly one predicted_taken bit with the accepted instruction
through if_id_t and id_ex_t. Since direct targets are computed from
that same instruction, use direction comparison rather than a full
saved-next-PC comparison. EX resolves the branch with forwarded operands
and the existing target/misalignment logic. For BRANCH/JAL recover on
a mismatch between predicted_taken and the effective resolved transfer
decision after misalignment suppression. Legal aligned JALR remains
unpredicted and redirects normally. Select the actual target when a
transfer is effective, otherwise the resolving instruction's own PC+4.
Preserve resolved EX/MEM.pc_next, jump link values, trap behavior and
RVFI even when the prediction was wrong. Correct predictions advance
without a control bubble; a direction mismatch for a target equal to
PC+4 may harmlessly trigger recovery.

Apply a prediction only when the fetch is actually accepted: imem is
ready, no load-use/dmem/divider hold is active, and no older recovery
kills it. Latch the prediction used on that edge, hold it with ID/EX
through hard holds, and clear it on bubbles. Train the selected counter
exactly once per advancing valid legal conditional branch, excluding
misalignment traps, toward its actual outcome with saturation. Use the
current counter for training and pre-edge table contents for a concurrent
lookup, with no update-to-lookup bypass. Prediction and the target adder
depend on raw fetch PC/data and table state, never on flush outputs.
Aliasing changes accuracy only and must not affect architectural state.

Reproducing 4201709 cycles at the current 46.095 MHz would yield about
109.71 iterations/second, a 6.9 percent fitness gain. Acceptance above
the 102.63 champion requires more than 107.35098 iterations/second,
equivalent to about 45.106 MHz at that cycle count. Predict a 10 percent
overall gain with medium confidence: the measured cycle benefit supplies
most of it, and removing recovery from the current decode-data critical
cone should preserve or modestly improve Fmax. This estimate is not a
measurement. The imem-to-PC adder, predictor mux, residual control fanout,
another arithmetic path or placement changes could still limit timing.

Validate through the unchanged formal, cocotb and cosimulation gates,
canonical 2K CoreMark CRCs/UART and both stall streams. Inspect Gowin's
paths to verify that EX recovery no longer reaches ID operand-data
inputs through instruction masking; judge success by median Gowin Fmax
times marker-delimited iterations/cycle, not by cycle saving alone.
Preserve nret=1, all ports, decoder legality and trap rules, M-extension
real and ALTOPS behavior, memory bounds and every evaluation invariant.

title: Flatten the ALU and EX result-selection network
motivation:
The champion scores 116.47 at a median 52.313 MHz. Earlier micro_opt
attempts targeted division or redirect feedback; the latest champion
already isolates divider completion and keeps redirect out of decode
payload enables. A fresh unmodified Gowin placement-option-0 run
reproduces 48.369 MHz and the reported 25.969 ns worst arrival. Its
detailed path traverses the signed multiplier mul_ss_63_s0 and then
seven successive n796 result-selection LUTs before the final EX hold
logic and dmem address input. These downstream selects contribute
approximately 6.05 ns after the DSP output, before the final hold mux.
This makes late result selection a concrete local timing target rather
than another predictor or divider-latency experiment.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the combinational ALU result-selection chain and its adjacent
EX jump/divide override muxes with mutually exclusive result masks and
explicitly balanced bitwise-OR reductions. Keep every arithmetic
operator and pipeline boundary unchanged. This is one local selection
topology optimization; it must add no instruction cycles or state.

In alu.sv compute integer, shift, compare, and multiply candidate values
independently. Decode the five-bit op into exact equality selects for
the supported combinational operations. Mask each 32-bit candidate with
its replicated select and combine candidates in small balanced groups,
followed by a balanced OR of those groups. Avoid a priority if/else
chain, a running OR accumulator, or a serial ternary chain. Unsupported
op values, including DIV/REM on the combinational output, still produce
zero. Keep the three existing multiply expressions and their signed
widths unchanged; the target is selection after the arithmetic, not a
change to multiplication or division algorithms. Under
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS use the exact existing substitute expressions as
candidates under the same operation masks.

In ex_stage.sv similarly form disjoint selectors for the normal ALU
result, PC+4 jump link, and completed divide result. Preserve the
existing priority exactly: divide first, then jump, then normal ALU.
Use masked candidates and a balanced OR into reg_q.alu_result, keeping
reset, stall retention, execute_wait bubbles, and all other EX fields
unchanged. Do not move redirect into payload enables or gate arithmetic
with retirement validity. Branch resolution, misalignment traps,
forwarding, retained WB availability, divider request/completion
handshakes, and the nret=1 interface retain their current behavior.

The expected gain is 12 percent in fitness from Fmax alone, with the
same marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. This is initially an unmeasured
prediction. Gowin may already optimize some case arms in parallel,
may reassociate an OR tree unfavorably, or may expose divider feedback
as the next limit. Confirm the actual reduction in post-arithmetic
LUT depth with vendor reports; do not rely on source-code appearance.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 121.82762, more than
4.6 percent above 116.47, using median vendor Fmax and measured cycles.

Preserve every existing check and all decoder legality rules. Exercise
all combinational ALU operations and unassigned op values with exact
integer references, including signed/high-half multiply boundaries and
all shift amounts. Run the existing real and ALTOPS arithmetic suites,
pipeline tests, formal and cosimulation gates, and canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/marker checks under both bus stalls. Check that cycle counts
and division latency remain unchanged and that jump-link and divide
results still forward correctly through stalled dependent consumers.

title: Resolve forwarding before the ID/EX operand registers
motivation:
The champion scores 116.47 at 52.313 MHz median Fmax and 4491485
marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md and the structural entries
in log.jsonl show that divider isolation and validity-only squashing
removed earlier timing bottlenecks. A fresh make timing TARGET=bench
reproduced its placement-option-0 result of 48.369 MHz. The detailed
25.969 ns path starts at register-file BSRAM output, passes through ID
data selection, several EX forwarding/operand muxes, the signed DSP
multiplier, and result selection before reaching the data-memory input.
The multiplier is only part of this path; operand selection precedes
every execute operation, including divider normalization and launch.

The champion scores 116.47 at 52.313 MHz median Fmax and 4491485
marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md and the structural entries
in log.jsonl show that divider isolation and validity-only squashing
removed earlier timing bottlenecks. A fresh make timing TARGET=bench
reproduced its placement-option-0 result of 48.369 MHz. The detailed

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move operand forwarding across the existing ID/EX register boundary.
Resolve each incoming instruction's register values in ID, capturing
fully forwarded source operands into ID/EX. EX then consumes those
registered values directly, without the existing EX/MEM-versus-MEM/WB
forwarding muxes ahead of arithmetic. This is one structural retiming
of operand delivery, with no added pipeline stage or instruction cycle.
Preserve the champion's validity-only squash and payload-hold rules.

For each raw ID source address, choose the youngest eligible producer:
first the instruction currently executing in EX, then the instruction
currently in MEM, then the register-file value with its existing WB
write-first bypass. Suppress x0 producers and force x0 reads to zero.
Compare against the corresponding current-stage destination tags, not
the old EX-forwarding stage ages. EX supplies its current combinational
architectural write value: ordinary ALU result, PC+4 for JAL/JALR, or
the completed divider result. A load in EX is unavailable and must
never forward its address as data. MEM supplies its aligned, extracted
and sign/zero-extended load value for loads, or its registered ALU
result otherwise. Both producer enables use valid and the stage's
trap-adjusted reg_write, so misaligned jumps or loads cannot inject a
write that architectural writeback suppresses.

Retain the existing conservative one-cycle load-use interlock. When
the immediately preceding load is in EX, hold the dependent fetch and
inject the existing ID/EX bubble. On the next eligible capture, that
load is in MEM and its actual load value enters the consumer's operand
register. Older dmem backpressure prevents capture until the bus is
ready. An outstanding divide also holds ID/EX; on its existing t8
completion transfer, its result can simultaneously supply the next
instruction's ID capture. Do not add a separate load or divide bypass
delay. WB write-first remains the oldest forwarding source.

Once ID/EX contains a valid instruction, its captured source operands
must already be complete and must remain unchanged through all backend
holds. This removes reliance on keeping a late forwarding source alive
while that consumer stalls. Keep divider operand snapshots and its
single-launch/result-retention protocol unchanged. Preserve the current
MEM/WB retention and retirement behavior; removing EX forwarding must
not replay older stores, writes or retirement. Use the captured source
values for EX comparisons, addresses, store data and RVFI. Repeated
redirects by a held branch and validity-only wrong-path squashing keep
their existing behavior. No path from redirect may enter raw source
addressing, the operand-data muxes or ID payload enables.

Make the register-file implementation compatible with an explicit
operand-capture boundary: retain the existing two asynchronous reads,
synchronous single write, reset-to-zero and write-first semantics, but
use flop storage rather than allowing Gowin to absorb the read/capture
network into BSRAM. A supported syn_ramstyle = "registers" attribute on
the array achieved this in the probe; an equivalent explicit register
bank is acceptable. This storage mapping is part of the operand-delivery
retiming, not a new architectural latency. It trades 930 extra
flip-flops and 765 LUTs for lower launch delay and a clean register
boundary. Keep ordinary portable RTL behavior in simulation and formal.
The unqualified RAM-inference version of the retimed probe stopped in
Gowin inference without producing reports, so do not depend on that
mapping. Do not introduce vendor primitives or change tool settings.

Export narrow result/producer interfaces from EX and MEM to ID, and
relocate the forwarding selection logic accordingly. The EX result tap
must depend only on registered ID/EX state, not the incoming ID operands;
the MEM tap depends on EX/MEM and memory data. This keeps the feedback
path synchronous and avoids combinational loops. EX must not retain
active late operand forwarding in addition to the new early network.
Leave ALU arithmetic, multiplier implementation, divider prefix and
seven iterations, ALTOPS formulas, decode rules, pipeline retirement
width and the exact top-level port contract unchanged.

An isolated RTL probe including trap-adjusted producer eligibility
passed the canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks with
exactly 4491485 measured cycles and no out-of-bounds access. It passed
eight full RVFI trace comparisons: selftest and random1/2/3, each with
ready buses and with both bus-stall modes enabled. Gowin Fmax was
56.747, 57.217 and 57.217 MHz for placement options 0, 1 and 2, giving
a 57.217 MHz median and estimated fitness 127.39, about 9.38 percent
above the champion. Area was 3556 LUTs, 1562 flip-flops, four BSRAMs
and six DSPs. The longest path moved inside the unchanged divider
recurrence. Formal was not run on the probe, and the implementation
still must pass all unchanged gates; this is not an accepted result.
A multiplier-only split was also probed, but exposed other operand and
divider paths and did not improve timing, supporting the broader shared
operand-delivery target rather than changing multiply latency.

Predict 10 percent higher fitness with medium confidence. The remaining
divider recurrence and the new EX-to-ID or MEM-to-ID capture paths may
limit the gain, and the larger register bank can increase routing cost.
Acceptance requires fitness above 121.82762; at unchanged CoreMark

title: A 16-entry agree predictor with validity-only recovery
motivation:
The previous 64-entry bimodal/JAL predictor reduced stalled CoreMark
cycles from 4491485 to 4201709, but its 48.244 MHz implementation lost
to the current 52.313 MHz, 116.47 iterations/second champion. That
predictor proposal cleared decoded control fields on recovery; the
current champion instead retains payload and controls and annuls only
validity, with side effects qualified locally. Preserve this timing
distinction when adding prediction. A software replay of the canonical
CoreMark ELF found 529588 conditional branches inside the markers.
A 16-entry ordinary bimodal table made 70409 direction errors; changing
its counters to learn agreement with a backward-taken/forward-not-taken
bias reduced this to 55134. That nearly matches the prior 64-entry
bimodal table's 51854 errors using one quarter of its counter storage.
Larger local-history predictors offered small extra savings, and tested
gshare variants were worse. This agree encoding addresses destructive
aliasing while keeping lookup, training and placement costs small.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact direct-control-flow predictor: a 16-entry agree table
of two-bit saturating counters indexed by fetch PC[5:2], plus early
prediction of legal JAL. For a legal conditional BRANCH, define its
static bias as instr[31]: backward branches biased taken, forward
branches biased not taken. The counter predicts whether the outcome
agrees with that bias, not the taken direction itself. Predict taken
when counter[1] == bias. Reset counters to weak agreement (2'b10),
which initially gives backward-taken/forward-not-taken prediction.
Sharing a counter between opposite-direction branches is constructive
when both usually follow their own bias. JAL is always predicted taken.
Extract B/J immediates from raw imem_data and share one PC-relative
target adder. Apply taken prediction only to word-aligned direct
targets. JALR and all other instructions remain sequential. Use no
BTB, return stack, global/local history, additional pipeline stage,
benchmark-specific PC information or ISA changes.

Keep the predictor physically small: 32 learned bits, a four-bit index,
and a single predicted_taken bit in each of if_id_t and id_ex_t. A pair
of 16-bit bitplanes is a suitable table representation. Lookup must
use pre-edge table state; do not forward an EX counter update into
fetch prediction. Train the currently stored counter once per advancing
legal conditional branch, excluding misalignment traps: saturating
increment if actual_taken == in.imm[31], otherwise saturating decrement.
Export the resolving instruction's four-bit PC index and agreement
outcome to IF; never train using the current fetch index or bias.
Train from current table state, not a stale saved counter. Aliasing
changes accuracy only. Do not expand the table in this hypothesis.

Apply the predicted successor only when fetch can advance: imem ready,
no load-use or backend hold, and no older recovery. Capture the exact
prediction used with the instruction. Prediction metadata is ordinary
payload: hold it with ID/EX through backend or load-use holds and allow
it to be meaningless when valid is zero. In particular, do not clear
decoded ctrl, operands, addresses, immediate, instruction, PC, or the
prediction bit in response to recovery. Retain the champion's existing
payload enable (!backend_hold && !load_use) and validity-only squash.
Preserve its raw fetch data, raw register-file source addresses,
recovery-independent load-use comparisons, and locally valid-qualified
forwarding, divider launch, memory effects and retirement.

EX computes effective_taken after the existing target-alignment check:
a legal conditional branch whose condition is true, or a legal jump,
with no misalignment fault. Recover when effective_taken differs from
the saved predicted_taken. This also gives ordinary recovery for JALR,
which is never predicted taken. A direction comparison is sufficient
because the only predicted targets are direct targets calculated from
the same instruction and PC. Set recovery_target to the effective
target if taken, otherwise the resolving instruction's own PC+4.
Preserve resolved EX/MEM.pc_next and all RVFI/link/trap behavior.
A correctly predicted branch or JAL must introduce no bubble.

Qualify recovery and training with !reset, in.valid, !stall_ex_mem and
!execute_wait, so a branch behind an older blocked memory transaction
cannot repeatedly train or redirect. Hold PC and ID/EX during that
backend hold. On release, correction overrides imem backpressure and
any younger fetch hold, sets PC to recovery_target, and annuls only
ID/EX.valid. imem unavailability otherwise injects an invalid entry
without accepting a prediction. Reset clears validity and initializes
prediction state. Adjacent branches, table collisions and simultaneous
lookup/training must retain the prediction actually used, even when
a table entry changes before that instruction resolves.

Expect roughly 6 percent fewer measured cycles and about 6 percent
higher fitness if Fmax stays near 52.313 MHz. The trace figures above
are direction-error counts from sequential architectural replay, not
cycle-accurate stalled simulation or FPGA measurements. Historical
64-entry cycle savings provide the performance anchor. At 4.22 million
cycles the candidate needs more than approximately 51.41 MHz to beat
116.47 by the required 4.6 percent. Reduced table size and retaining
validity-only recovery are intended to preserve that timing margin;
placement changes and the imem-to-target-adder path remain risks.

Validate with the unchanged formal, cocotb and cosimulation gates,
canonical CoreMark CRCs/UART, marker-only cycle counts and both stall
streams. Inspect median Gowin Fmax and its worst paths; fewer branch
bubbles alone is insufficient. Preserve nret=1 and the exact top-level
ports, decoder defaults, arithmetic including ALTOPS, memory bounds,
trap semantics and every existing correctness check.

title: Shorten the isolated divider recurrence with parallel radix-4 digits
motivation:
The champion scores 126.70 at 56.909 MHz with 4491485 marker-delimited
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from quotient_q[31] to
remainder_q[1] entirely inside u_ex/u_alu, with 129 cells and 22.480 ns
arrival. Four serial restoring subtract/select steps now limit timing
after early operand capture removed the preceding forwarding bottleneck.
The micro_opt history matters: hyp-20261002-001-r2s0 already raised its
parent's Fmax from 41.241 to 45.934 MHz using parallel radix-4 selection,
but lost that tournament to 46.095 MHz divider-completion isolation.
Its worst path moved into forwarding/redirect/hazard logic. Later
champions removed those control and operand paths. Combining radix-4
recurrence arithmetic with the current registered prefix/completion
boundaries therefore addresses a newly exposed bottleneck. This does
not repeat the unsuccessful ALU result-mux flattening from r4s0.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real divider's four serial one-bit restoring steps per
busy cycle with two serial two-bit radix-4 steps, each evaluating the
D, 2D and 3D subtraction candidates concurrently. Keep the current narrow
four-bit launch prefix, seven subsequent busy cycles, registered final
quotient/remainder, and earliest t8 result handshake exactly unchanged.
There is no final-iteration combinational bypass and no added pipeline
stage. The mechanism is reduced arithmetic depth inside one recurrence.

At accepted launch, retain the existing divisor magnitude D and capture
3D in a new unsigned 34-bit register using an explicitly widened D+2D
sum. Derive 2D from registered D by wiring. Preserve the existing prefix
calculation, including its small-divisor guard, quotient initialization,
and remainder initialization. Keep the multiple-generation adder out of
the iterative feedback path. Reset the added state with the divider.

In each radix-4 step let R be the 32-bit partial remainder and Q the
32-bit combined unconsumed-dividend/quotient shift register. Form the
unsigned 34-bit trial T={R,Q[31:30]}. In parallel compute unsigned
35-bit differences Xk={1'b0,T}-{1'b0,kD} for k=1,2,3; extend every
divisor multiple to 34 bits before subtraction. Define gk=!Xk[34].
Choose the largest non-borrowing candidate, or digit zero. For positive
D use disjoint selects s0=!g1, s1=g1&&!g2, s2=g2&&!g3, s3=g3 and
quotient digit {g2,g3||(g1&&!g2)}. Select the low 32 bits of T, X1,
X2 or X3 with these masks and a balanced OR. Feed that remainder and
Q_next={Q[29:0],digit} through a second identical digit step and capture
its outputs in the existing quotient_q and remainder_q registers.
Avoid a separate magnitude comparator followed by subtraction, and
avoid a serial priority mux across the three candidate remainders.

For D>0 the launch prefix establishes R<D and each step preserves it:
T<4D, so the chosen digit is 0..3 and its remainder fits in 32 bits.
Keep the full 34-bit trial/multiple widths through the borrow decision;
3*(2^32-1) must not overflow. D=0 may bypass this invariant because the
existing explicit divide-by-zero result override must remain intact.
Preserve signed magnitude preparation, quotient and remainder signs,
INT_MIN/-1 behavior, sticky completion under result backpressure, reset
cancellation, and launch operand snapshots. Preserve the exact ALTOPS
arithmetic and its identical request/completion timing. All other ALU
operations, EX integration, early forwarding, pipeline controls, nret=1,
top-level ports, decoder legality and verification checks stay intact.

An isolated RTL probe of this exact recurrence change, using copies of
the current champion sources and the unchanged vendor evaluation flow,
measured Gowin Fmax of 65.576, 65.345 and 65.345 MHz for placement
options 0, 1 and 2. The median is 65.345 MHz. It used 3776 LUTs and
1595 flip-flops, increases of 184 and 33, with the same four BSRAMs
and six DSPs. The option-0 recurrence path fell to 71 cells and
20.502 ns arrival; divider launch and multiplication are now near the
timing limit, with the worst path at 20.544 ns. These are reported
arrival times, not clock periods; use the vendor Fmax for fitness.

The probe passed the complete existing ALU cocotb suite, including real
signed/unsigned division, launch-prefix state checks, t8 handshake,
operand isolation, reset and held completion. All eight full RVFI trace
comparisons passed: selftest and random1/2/3, each with ready buses and
with both instruction/data stalls. The canonical stalled CoreMark run
passed CRC/UART/marker validation with no out-of-bounds access and exactly
4491485 bracketed cycles (start 15801, stop 4507286). Thus the probe's
measured Fmax and iterations/cycle imply fitness 145.49, approximately
14.83 percent above 126.70. Formal and formal-deep were not run on this
probe; implementation must still pass every unchanged gate. Only the
hypothesis is delivered; the experiment did not modify production RTL.

Predict 15 percent higher fitness with medium confidence. Extra
subtractors and candidate routing increase area, and the exposed launch
and multiplication paths cap further gains. Use median Gowin timing
across placement options and actual marker-delimited cycles; acceptance
requires fitness above 132.5282, more than 4.6 percent over 126.70.
At unchanged cycles this requires approximately 59.526 MHz median Fmax.
Preserve the demonstrated local scope and divider latency.

Validate real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU with existing unit tests plus widened
multiple, digit-threshold and prefix-boundary vectors and deterministic
random operands. Verify exact t8 earliest handshake, held completion,
changing live operands after launch, reset and consecutive requests.
Run unchanged formal and cosimulation gates, and require canonical
CoreMark CRCs, UART validation and marker checks under both bus stalls.
ALTOPS formal does not validate the new arithmetic; retain real-divider
tests and the existing formal-deep correctness obligation.

title: Replace serial divider recurrence with a parallel radix-16 digit engine
motivation:
The champion scores 126.70 at 56.909 MHz and 4491485 marker-delimited
CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path now runs entirely inside the
divider, from quotient_q[31] to remainder_q[1], with 129 cells and a
22.480 ns arrival time. LESSONS.md and the structural history show that
registered completion and early operand capture removed the surrounding
EX and forwarding bottlenecks. The remaining recurrence still chains
four full-width restoring subtract/select operations in every cycle.
The earlier micro_opt radix-4 candidate, hyp-20261002-001-r2s0, reached
45.934 MHz from 41.241 MHz but exposed forwarding/redirect feedback;
it predates those structural fixes and is not evidence that the current
recurrence is already fast enough. Target the divider's recurrence
architecture with one four-bit digit selected in parallel.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the real divider's four cascaded one-bit restoring steps with
one radix-16 quotient-digit engine backed by registered divisor
multiples. Keep the existing narrow four-bit launch prefix, seven
subsequent recurrence cycles, registered completion, and earliest t8
result handshake. This is one structural substitution of the divider
datapath: a bank of parallel candidates replaces serial quotient-bit
decisions. Ordinary execution and instruction scheduling stay intact.

At request acceptance capture the positive divisor magnitude D and
its multiples k*D for k=1..15, each explicitly unsigned and 36 bits.
Multiples must be registered before the first recurrence cycle; do
not calculate them in the remainder-feedback path. The measured probe
derived multiple 1 from divisor_q and clocked multiples 2..15 from
constant shift/add/subtract expressions in a generated bank, allowing
synthesis to share equivalent register bits. Use 3D=2D+D, 5D=4D+D,
7D=8D-D, 9D=8D+D, 11D=8D+2D+D, 13D=16D-2D-D and 15D=16D-D;
even multiples are shifts of the corresponding expressions. All these
expressions use the request's widened D, not previous registered
multiples. Avoid variable multipliers and division operators. In
particular, 15*(2^32-1) must not overflow.
Retain the existing original dividend, signedness, zero-divisor flag,
normalized quotient state and launch-prefix initialization. A large
divisor must never be truncated into the narrow-prefix network.

Each busy cycle forms the 36-bit trial T={remainder_q,quotient_q[31:28]}.
In parallel compute the fifteen 37-bit differences Xk={1'b0,T}-
{1'b0,multiple_k_q}. Their top bits indicate borrow. For D>0 the
successful-subtraction bits gk=!Xk[36] are monotonic. Select digit 0
if g1 is false, digit k for gk && !g(k+1), or digit 15 if g15 is true.
Build a mutually exclusive selection and balanced OR reduction for
both the selected remainder and four-bit quotient digit; avoid a
fifteen-deep priority chain. The probe masked sixteen 36-bit bundles
{candidate_remainder[31:0],digit[3:0]} and reduced them through explicit
16-to-8-to-4-to-2-to-1 OR levels. Candidate zero is T itself. Only after
the full-width borrow decision may the selected remainder be truncated
to 32 bits. Update remainder_q with that selected remainder and
quotient_q with {quotient_q[27:0],digit} on the existing iteration edge.
For nonzero D, R<D implies T<16*D, so digit 0..15 suffices and the
new remainder is again below D and fits in 32 bits.

Leave result selection, signed correction and divide-by-zero override
driven solely by registered completed state. Preserve all DIV/DIVU/
REM/REMU semantics, including INT_MIN/-1 and dividend-signed remainder.
The zero-divisor override remains authoritative even though the normal
recurrence invariant only applies to positive divisors. Keep the exact
ALTOPS formulas and identical real/ALTOPS handshake timing. Completed
state freezes under backpressure; reset cancels active and completed
requests. EX retains its single-launch, drain-older-stages and exact-once
transfer protocol without adding launch or correction cycles. Preserve
nret=1, the top-level interface, all traps and every existing invariant.

The prediction is higher Fmax with unchanged CoreMark cycles: fifteen
parallel subtractors and a balanced selection replace four dependent
carry/selection chains. The costs are a larger arithmetic bank,
registered divisor multiples and higher remainder fanout. Launch-time
magnitude/multiple generation or ordinary multiplication may become
the next bottleneck, and routing may reduce the theoretical gain.
Predict 20 percent higher fitness with medium confidence, based on
the probe described below. Acceptance requires fitness above 132.5282; at the
champion's cycle count this requires median Fmax above 59.525 MHz.

A temporary RTL probe passed Verilator lint, the existing real ALU
and ALTOPS suites, and an added real-arithmetic test for all radix-16
digit thresholds, repeated/mixed quotient digits, wide multiples and
sign combinations. An independent recurrence model also matched exact
integer division for 450180 valid remainder/divisor/nibble cases.
Eight full RVFI trace comparisons passed: selftest and random1/2/3,
each with ready buses and with both bus-stall modes enabled. The
canonical stalled CoreMark run passed CRC/UART/bracketing checks,
made no out-of-bounds accesses, and retained exactly 4491485 measured

title: Compact agree prediction with registered EX operands
motivation:
The current champion takes 4491485 marker-delimited CoreMark cycles at
56.909 MHz, scoring 126.70 iterations/second. The predictor history in
LESSONS.md and log.jsonl establishes a repeatable cycle-count benefit:
the 64-entry bimodal predictor took 4201709 cycles, and r4s2's 16-entry
agree predictor took 4203513, a 6.41 percent reduction. Both lost on
timing. In r4s2 the worst path ran from the register file through ID,
EX and the ALU to dmem; its 48.401 MHz result used the previous operand
forwarding topology. The r4s1 champion now captures fully forwarded
operands in ID/EX and forces register-file flop storage. Its worst
path is internal to the divider, from quotient_q to remainder_q.
That changed timing boundary is the reason to retry compact prediction;
merely shrinking or renaming the previously failed predictor is not.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one early direct-control-flow predictor to the current champion:
a 16-entry, two-bit agree table indexed by fetch PC[5:2], with early
direct JAL prediction. Preserve the champion's complete forwarded
operand capture and flop register file. Use exactly 32 learned bits
and one predicted_taken bit in each of if_id_t and id_ex_t. Do not
add a BTB, return stack, history register, instruction cache, pipeline
stage, or arithmetic change. The objective is to obtain the already
measured control-bubble reduction without reopening the old long
register-file/forwarding/EX path.

For a legal conditional branch, use instr[31] as its static bias:
backward taken, forward not taken. Each saturating counter learns
agreement with that bias. Reset counters to weak agreement (2'b10);
predict taken when counter[1] == instr[31]. Increment toward 2'b11
when the resolved direction equals the resolving branch's imm[31],
and decrement toward 2'b00 otherwise. Use current stored state for
training, the resolving PC[5:2] for the write index, and pre-edge state
for lookup. Never bypass a same-cycle EX update into fetch prediction.
Two 16-bit bitplanes keep the lookup and write network small.

Predecode the raw fetch word independently of validity and correction.
Recognize BRANCH only for funct3 in {0,1,4,5,6,7}, and recognize JAL
by its exact opcode. Predict legal JAL unconditionally taken. Extract
B/J immediates and use one shared PC-relative target adder. Apply taken
prediction only for a word-aligned direct target. JALR and other
instructions predict sequentially. Keep imem_addr driven by the PC
register; predictor outputs must not replace raw imem_data, alter
out.valid = imem_ready, or enter register-file source-address logic.

On normal fetch advancement, choose the predicted target or PC+4.
An accepted instruction requires imem ready, no load-use or backend
hold, and no older correction; only then does that predicted successor
take effect. Capture predicted_taken as ordinary ID/EX payload under
the existing !backend_hold && !load_use enable. It holds with operands
on a backend hold, and is inert when valid is zero. Preserve the
leading pc/rs1_val/rs2_val fields and valid as the last struct field,
since existing tests check this registered operand boundary directly.
Corrections must annul only validity, never decoded controls, source
addresses, operands, immediates, or prediction payload.

Resolve branches using the existing registered EX operands. Define
effective_taken as a legal taken conditional branch or legal jump,
after the existing misaligned-target check. For a valid advancing
control transfer, correct only when effective_taken differs from the
saved predicted_taken. Direction comparison suffices: predicted
targets are exact PC-relative targets from the same fetched instruction,
and JALR is never predicted taken. A correct direct prediction produces
no flush. A predicted-taken branch resolving not-taken corrects to its
own PC+4. An unpredicted taken branch or JALR corrects to its resolved
target. Keep EX/MEM.pc_next architectural and independent of prediction,
including PC+4 fallback on a target-misalignment trap, and retain jump
link and trap-adjusted forwarding behavior.

Use a valid, legal control transfer advancing from EX as the correction
event: !reset && in.valid && !stall_ex_mem, qualified by branch/jump
controls. Train once on that event for conditional branches without
a misalignment fault, including correctly predicted branches. An older
stalled memory operation holds the branch and its prediction and defers
both training and correction until release. Correction then overrides
imem backpressure and younger fetch holds, updates PC and clears only
ID/EX.valid. A control transfer cannot be an executing DIV/REM, so do
not route divider completion or execute_wait through the correction
or training cone merely to express this redundant condition. Ordinary
fetch still obeys the existing backend_hold and load-use interlocks.
Adjacent branches and counter aliases must use the prediction captured
at their own acceptance, even if that table entry changes afterward.

Keep recovery out of payload enables and forwarding selection. Retain
reg_file.sv's syn_ramstyle = "registers", the EX/MEM-to-ID forwarding
network, and fully resolved ID/EX operands. Do not import the prior
predictor's older forwarding implementation. Prediction must remain
off ALU result selection, divider request/completion, and memory data
paths. Aliasing may change accuracy only, never architectural behavior.
Preserve nret=1, top-level ports, decoder legality, all arithmetic and
ALTOPS semantics, bus handshakes, and every existing invariant/check.

Expect approximately 6 percent higher fitness; this is an unmeasured
estimate for the new combination. At the prior agree predictor's
4203513 cycles and unchanged 56.909 MHz, fitness would be about 135.38,
a 6.85 percent gain. Acceptance requires strictly more than 132.5282
iterations/second, or about 55.71 MHz at that cycle count. Thus only
about 2.1 percent Fmax loss is affordable. Added fetch-adder delay,
placement effects on the divider, and the newly combinational
EX-to-ID forwarding path are the principal risks; smaller state alone
did not solve them in r4s2. Compare median Gowin timing and actual
marker-delimited cycles, not RVFI-only logic or direction accuracy.

Validate through the unchanged cocotb, formal and cosimulation gates,
canonical CoreMark CRCs and UART text, both approximately 22 percent
stall streams, and the existing marker timing contract. Exercise
correct prediction and both correction directions with independent
imem/dmem holds, load-dependent branches, adjacent control transfers,
reset, illegal encodings and misaligned targets. Require no wrong-path
memory effects, no duplicate training on held branches, exact RVFI
operands and successors, and monotonic retirement order. Retain the
current tests proving complete, stable forwarded ID/EX operands.

title: Bypass EX operand muxes for RV32M arithmetic
motivation:
The champion scores 152.61 iterations/s at median 68.545 MHz, with
4491485 marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md records that
registered forwarded operands and the parallel radix-16 divider
moved the bottleneck to ordinary EX arithmetic and result selection.
The current EX still feeds every arithmetic unit through the AUIPC
PC-versus-rs1 and immediate-versus-rs2 operand muxes. Every legal
RV32M operation uses rs1 and rs2, so those muxes are unnecessary on
multiplier and divider paths. Their delay and shared fanout affect
both multiplication and divider launch. The r4s0 micro_opt result
warns against another global result-mux rewrite; specialize the
arithmetic inputs instead, retaining the existing execution timing.

title: Separate M-extension launch preparation from registered multiply completion
motivation:
The champion scores 152.61 iterations/s at 68.545 MHz and 4491485
marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
ID/EX rs2_val[15], passes through EX arithmetic/result selection, and
ends at dmem, with 20.661 ns arrival time. LESSONS.md and the structural
history show that early operand capture and the parallel radix-16
recurrence removed earlier bottlenecks. The r4s1 multiplier-only probe
failed while other paths dominated. A fresh multiplier-only probe on
this champion also failed: the divider's launch normalization/prefix
became critical and median Fmax fell to 57.299 MHz. The promising
structural angle is therefore to isolate M-extension arithmetic at its
launch/completion boundaries, addressing the exposed launch dependency
as part of moving multiplication out of single-cycle EX.
