hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate M-extension launch preparation and completed-result delivery
from the ordinary single-cycle execute path. Give MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU
a registered product boundary, and make the existing divider's narrow
launch prefix independent of full-width magnitude normalization. This
is one structural redesign of the M-unit timing boundaries. It changes
neither the instruction pipeline depth nor the existing divide schedule.
Both parts are necessary: the isolated multiplier and isolated prefix
probes below each lose to the champion.

Launch multiplication directly from fully forwarded ID/EX rs1 and rs2,
without the AUIPC/immediate operand muxes. Form one signed 33-by-33
product: extend A with its sign for MULH/MULHSU and zero otherwise;
extend B with its sign for MULH and zero otherwise. Explicitly cast
both operands to signed 33-bit values and capture a signed 66-bit
product plus a high/low selector at request edge t0. After this register,
select bits 31:0 for MUL or 63:32 for the three high-half operations.
This gives exact signed/unsigned results without serial high-half sign
correction. Remove the active combinational MUL paths from the ordinary
ALU result. The first possible EX/MEM acceptance is t1, costing one
extra cycle per multiply except where an older memory hold hides it.

Use a single-outstanding request/completion protocol. EX launches a
valid legal multiply exactly once, holds PC and ID/EX through the
existing execute_wait interlock, and lets older stages drain. Once an
older EX/MEM entry advances, emit invalid bubbles while waiting; retain
an older stalled memory request under the existing dmem hold instead.
A multiply may launch during that hold because its captured source
values are complete. Retain product, selector and completion until
EX/MEM accepts them, then consume exactly once. Reset cancels pending
work. Forward only completed products, including to a dependent ID
capture on the completion transfer edge. Preserve source snapshots,
x0, producer age priority, trap eligibility and exact RVFI retirement.
Keep multiply and divide completion state independent so consecutive
and mixed M operations cannot consume the wrong result.

The divider launch must not serialize a 32-bit absolute value into four
restoring prefix steps. Keep full-width magnitude generation for the
quotient's lower bits and registered divisor multiples, but prepare the
leading nibble and small-divisor decision in parallel from raw ALU
operands A and B. Let negA = signed_op && A[31], and likewise negB,
where signed_op identifies DIV/REM. Compute the four-bit leading
magnitude nibble N as A[31:28] when positive, or
(~A[31:28] + (A[27:0] == 0)) modulo 16 when negative. The lower-bit
zero reduction supplies the only carry needed by this high nibble.
Compute four-bit D as B[3:0], or -B[3:0] modulo 16 when negB.
The exact nonzero-small-divisor predicate is B[3:0] != 0 and either
all B[31:4] bits equal one when negB, or all equal zero otherwise.
Thus magnitudes 1..15 are recognized without a 32-bit negate/comparison;
zero and magnitude 16 or larger never enter the small-divisor path.

Replace the four dependent restoring-prefix cells with a complete
combinational 256-entry, eight-bit constant map keyed by {D,N}.
For D=1..15, the output is {N modulo D, floor(N/D)}, each four bits.
For D=0 define it as {N,4'b0}; the existing zero-divisor result override
remains authoritative. Emit literal constants in a complete case table,
not runtime division or remainder operators. On request acceptance,
initialize quotient_q to {dividend_magnitude[27:0], small ? Q4 : 4'b0}
and remainder_q to {28'b0, small ? R4 : N}. Preserve the existing
registered 36-bit divisor multiples, seven subsequent radix-16
iterations, earliest t8 result handshake, sign correction, sticky
completion and all division corner cases. Large divisors must not be
truncated into the lookup. Keep portable combinational semantics if
Gowin infers a ROM and absorbs the existing capture register; do not
add a ROM cycle or use vendor-only primitives.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, capture the existing exact MUL-family XOR
formulas behind the same new request/wait/completion timing. Keep the
existing division ALTOPS formulas and divider controller schedule.
Preserve nret=1, every core port, decoder legality, alignment traps,
register-file mapping, validity-only recovery, memory handshakes and
all hard invariants. No predictor, cache, extra instruction stage or
other architectural change is part of this hypothesis.

A temporary combined RTL probe passed Verilator lint, eight full RVFI
trace comparisons (selftest and random1/2/3, each with ready buses and
with both stall modes), and the canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/
marker checks without out-of-bounds accesses. CoreMark took 4585465
measured cycles, 2.09 percent more than the champion. Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 reached 72.133/73.509/73.509 MHz, giving a 73.509 MHz
median and estimated fitness 160.3087, 5.0447 percent above 152.61.
Area was 4551 LUTs, 1919 flip-flops, five BSRAMs and two DSPs. The

title: Compact agree prediction on the parallel-divider champion
motivation:
The champion still fetches sequentially and loses one acceptance opportunity
on every taken branch or jump: its IF/ID bundle is combinational, so there
is only one younger instruction to squash. LESSONS.md and the predictor
entries in experiments/log.jsonl provide repeatable evidence for reducing
this cost. The 64-entry bimodal predictor took 4201709 measured CoreMark
cycles; the 16-entry agree predictor took 4203513 versus 4491485 without
prediction. The larger table saved only another 0.043 percent of cycles.

Most decisively, hyp-20261002-003-r5s2 combined compact agree prediction
with fully forwarded ID/EX operands and flop register-file storage. It
passed formal and cosimulation, reduced cycles by 6.41 percent and raised
median Fmax from 56.909 to 57.470 MHz. Its regression label means it lost
the tournament to the parallel-divider candidate, not that prediction
hurt its parent. It retained the old divider recurrence and scored 136.72.
The current r5s1 champion already removes that bottleneck, scoring 152.61
at 68.545 MHz with the original 4491485 cycles. Applying the demonstrated
small predictor to this new base is the best-supported predictor angle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one early direct-control-flow predictor to the supplied champion:
a 16-entry two-bit agree table indexed by fetch PC[5:2], including early
direct JAL prediction. Preserve the current parallel radix-16 divider,
registered divisor multiples, t8 completion handshake, fully forwarded
ID/EX operands, and syn_ramstyle = "registers" register-file storage.
This is a predictor-only change; do not transplant an older core or add
a BTB, return stack, global history, cache, pipeline stage, or ALU change.

Store the 32 learned bits as two 16-bit counter bitplanes. For a legal
conditional branch, use instr[31] as the static taken bias: backward
taken, forward not taken. Reset each counter to weak agreement (2'b10).
Predict taken when its counter MSB equals that branch's instr[31].
Increment toward 2'b11 when the resolved direction agrees with the
resolving branch's imm[31], and decrement toward 2'b00 otherwise.
Update the current stored counter at the resolving PC[5:2]; do not
overwrite it from an old lookup snapshot. Use pre-edge state for a
simultaneous lookup and update, without an EX-to-fetch update bypass.

Predecode raw imem_data independently of recovery and readiness.
Recognize BRANCH only for funct3 in {0,1,4,5,6,7}; recognize JAL by its
exact opcode and predict it taken unconditionally. Extract the B/J
immediate and use one shared PC-relative target adder. Predict taken
only for a word-aligned direct target. JALR and all other instructions,
including reserved branch encodings, predict sequentially. imem_addr
remains driven by the PC register; out.instr remains raw imem_data and
out.valid remains imem_ready. Do not substitute instructions or gate
register-file addresses, load-use comparisons, or forwarding data with
predictor decisions or recovery.

Add just one predicted_taken bit to if_id_t and id_ex_t. A full predicted
target and wide target comparator are unnecessary: every taken prediction
uses the exact PC-relative target of its own instruction, and JALR is
unpredicted. Capture the bit as ordinary payload alongside that instruction
under the existing !backend_hold && !load_use enable, holding it with the
operands across backend stalls. Preserve the leading ID/EX pc, rs1_val
and rs2_val fields and valid as the final field for the existing operand
boundary checks. Invalid payload, including prediction metadata, is inert.

Advance the PC to the predicted target or PC+4 only on normal accepted
fetches: imem ready, no load-use or backend hold, and no older recovery.
Recovery has priority over those younger fetch restrictions. In EX use
the existing registered operands and target-alignment checks to compute
effective_taken for a legal branch/jump. On a valid advancing control
transfer, recover only if effective_taken differs from its saved
predicted_taken. Correct direct predictions neither squash nor bubble.
A predicted-taken branch resolving not-taken recovers to its own PC+4;
an unpredicted taken branch or aligned JALR recovers to its actual target.
A direction mismatch when the target equals PC+4 may harmlessly recover.
Keep EX/MEM.pc_next architectural, independent of prediction, including
the existing PC+4 fallback and link-write suppression on alignment traps.

Qualify recovery and training with !reset, in.valid, legal branch/jump
controls, and !stall_ex_mem. Train only conditional branches without a
target-misalignment fault, exactly once as they advance from EX, including
correctly predicted branches. An older dmem hold preserves the resolving
instruction and its prediction and defers both events until release.
Recovery on release must override imem unavailability and annul the
younger instruction even if its raw word changes while unavailable.
A legal control transfer cannot simultaneously be DIV/REM, so keep
divider completion and execute_wait out of recovery/training logic;
normal fetch and payload capture still obey the existing backend hold.
Adjacent branches and aliased entries must resolve against the prediction
actually captured for each instruction, even if the table changes later.

Recovery may affect only PC selection and ID/EX validity. Keep the
champion's ID payload enables, source-data paths, local valid-qualified
effects, EX/MEM forwarding, load-use interlocks, and divider controls
intact. Keep predictor state and logic out of ALU/result selection and
dmem data paths. In particular, preserve the parallel divider verbatim;
this hypothesis adds the missing control-bubble reduction to its timing
improvement rather than reimplementing arithmetic. Preserve nret=1,
every top-level port, decoder legality, ALTOPS semantics and all checks.

The expected fitness gain is about 7 percent, conditional on retaining
timing. Repeating 4203513 cycles at 68.545 MHz would yield 163.066
iterations/second, about 6.85 percent above 152.61. This combination has
not been measured. Acceptance requires strictly more than 159.63006
iterations/second; at that cycle count Fmax must exceed 67.1007 MHz.
Thus the affordable Fmax loss is only about 2.1 percent. The champion's
recorded worst path now starts at registered rs2_val and runs through
EX/ALU toward dmem, so added placement/routing pressure and the new fetch
target path are real risks even though r5s2 preserved its parent's Fmax.
Judge the actual median Gowin Fmax times marker-delimited throughput,
not table accuracy or cycle reduction alone.

Validate with the unchanged formal, cocotb and cosimulation gates and
canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART success text, timing markers, and both
approximately 22 percent bus-stall streams. Directed tests must check
warmup and both correction directions, colliding forward/backward

control flow following a held divide, correction during imem stalls,
branches held behind dmem operations, and simultaneous lookup/training.
Require exact retirement PCs, actual successors, operands, links, traps
and consecutive order; wrong-path stores must never reach the bus.
Check that a warmed no-wait taken loop has no taken-branch bubbles and
that a held branch trains only once when it advances. Retain all tests
proving complete and stable forwarded ID/EX operands.

title: Direct RV32M operands on the agree-predictor champion
motivation:
The current champion scores 161.18 iterations/s at 67.751 MHz and
4203513 marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts
at cpu/u_id/reg_q.ctrl.is_auipc_s0 and ends at the divider's
remainder_q_3_s1: 20.560 ns through EX operand selection and the ALU.
Every RV32M instruction uses two register operands, yet its arithmetic
still receives the generic AUIPC/PC and immediate/register mux outputs.
These unnecessary muxes introduce control delay before multiplication,
signed normalization, the launch prefix and divisor-multiple generation.

LESSONS.md and experiments/log.jsonl provide direct evidence for this
specific micro_opt. hyp-20261002-001-r6s0 bypassed those muxes on the
previous parallel-divider champion, improving median Fmax from 68.545
to 72.222 MHz with identical 4491485 cycles and passing formal/cosim.
Its 160.80 fitness lost to the predictor candidate's 161.18; the
regression label does not mean the routing change hurt its own parent.
The current champion contains that winning predictor but still lacks
the operand bypass. Its AUIPC-control-to-divider path makes applying
this demonstrated local optimization especially well motivated.

title: Pipeline M-unit launch and multiply delivery without global multiply stalls
motivation:
The champion scores 161.18 iterations/s at 67.751 MHz and 4203513
marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
ID/EX ctrl.is_auipc and ends in divider remainder initialization.
LESSONS.md and the structural log show that moving arithmetic across
register boundaries has helped, but r6s1's registered multiplier forced
an extra cycle on every MUL and raised CoreMark cycles by 2.09 percent.
That candidate reached 73.119 MHz but missed acceptance. Preserve its
necessary separation of divider launch preparation while placing the
multiply product in the existing EX/MEM pipeline instead of holding
all issue until multiplication completes. This targets both the timing
boundary and the unnecessary scheduling cost of that M-unit design.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the M-unit launch/result boundaries: multiply progresses
through EX/MEM and supplies its result in MEM, while divider launch uses
its own direct-source narrow initialization path. This is one structural
M-unit redesign. It retains the existing instruction-stage count,
predictor, register-file mapping and nret=1. Do not introduce a global
multiply wait, scoreboard, out-of-order retirement or new memory state.

At the existing EX/MEM edge, capture a signed 66-bit product computed
from signed 33-bit operands derived directly from the fully forwarded
ID/EX rs1_val and rs2_val. Extend A with its sign only for MULH/MULHSU;
extend B with its sign only for MULH; zero-extend otherwise. Explicitly
cast both 33-bit operands signed before multiplying. Carry an is_multiply
bit and a high/low selector with the EX/MEM payload. Product capture,
metadata and instruction validity must use the same EX/MEM advancement,
bubble and downstream-hold rules. This permits one independent multiply
per cycle and introduces no separate request/completion controller.

In MEM, select product[31:0] for MUL or product[63:32] for MULH/MULHSU/
MULHU. This single extended product gives exact signed and unsigned
results without post-product subtraction. Feed the selected value to
both the MEM-to-ID forwarding tap and MEM/WB architectural-result field.
Remove active multiplication from the ordinary EX ALU result/mux path;
only the dedicated product register captures the raw multiply output.
Do not route an unregistered product through EX-to-ID forwarding.

Generalize the existing conservative EX-load dependency predicate to
include valid legal EX multiplies. An unavailable nonzero destination
matching either incoming raw source field holds fetch and inserts the
existing ID/EX bubble. Backend holds retain priority. Exclude EX
multiplies from the EX producer enable. A dependent instruction then

still overrides an older product. Keep divider execute_wait unchanged.

the rest of the payload. A divider wait may drain an older multiply
normally and then replace it with an invalid bubble. Multiplication
must never assert a memory request; load/store instructions continue to

multiplies remain inert, and source snapshots/RVFI values come from the

legality, validity-only recovery and exact-once single-channel retirement.

multiplier's timing benefit: a multiply-only probe on this champion fell

and constants. Capture their result at the product boundary and expose

representation stores the 32-bit ALTOPS value in both product halves.

Move every existing real multiplication arithmetic vector to a harness
that exercises the new clocked path; do not discard vector coverage.
The old pipeline assertion of bubble-free immediate MUL dependence must
be replaced by an exact one-bubble assertion, retaining all result,
source, memory-effect and order assertions and adding an independent

An exploratory combined RTL probe passed eight full RVFI trace
comparisons: selftest and random1/2/3, each with ready buses and with both
stall modes. Canonical stalled CoreMark passed CRC/UART/marker checks
with no out-of-bounds access and 4239051 measured cycles, 0.8454 percent
above the champion. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 reached
68.423/72.993/72.993 MHz, for a 72.993 MHz median and estimated fitness
172.19184, 6.832 percent above 161.18. Area was 4761 LUTs, 1951 flip-flops,
five BSRAMs and two DSPs. The reported worst path moved into the existing
divider recurrence. These are probe measurements, not an accepted
evaluation. The pipeline suite passed after replacing the immediate-MUL
zero-bubble assertion with its exact one-bubble counterpart and adding
149 operand pairs across all four multiply kinds, with and without
stalls. Independent multiplies retired in consecutive cycles. Formal
and formal-deep have not been run. An additional ALU-level probe passed
7296 real division vectors and the same 7296 ALTOPS vectors, checking
launch state, seven iterations, t8 consumption, changed live operands
and completed-result backpressure. These include every prefix nibble,
signed carry boundaries and large-divisor aliases.

Predict 7 percent higher fitness with medium confidence. Routing and
the remaining divider recurrence may consume the margin. Require all

then all three Gowin placements. Acceptance requires fitness above
168.59428, equivalent to median Fmax above 71.467975 MHz at the measured
4239051 cycles. Preserve every hard invariant and all evaluation files.

title: Precompute direct-control recovery addresses beside the predictor
motivation:
The current champion already has the successful 16-entry agree predictor
and early JAL. Previous predictor experiments report 4203513 CoreMark
cycles for this design versus 4201709 for a 64-entry bimodal predictor,
so simply enlarging the table offers negligible throughput improvement.
A fresh reference-interpreter profile of the canonical timed region has
2922016 retired instructions, 529588 conditional branches, and only 13735
JALRs, all returns. An immediate-update trace model of the current agree
policy misses approximately 55124 branches. These are architectural
profile counts, not a cycle-accurate RTL measurement. They suggest that
accuracy-only prediction has too little headroom to clear 4.6 percent.

The remaining predictor opportunity is recovery timing and duplication.
Fetch already computes each direct target and PC+4, but EX recomputes
those addresses before selecting recovery and jump-link results. Carrying
prepared recovery endpoints across ID/EX can remove this repeated
arithmetic from control recovery while keeping the proven predictor.
The champion's reported worst path is in EX/ALU divider launch, not
fetch, so improvement from this change is uncertain and must be measured.

direct-control recovery address generation across ID/EX. In fetch form

title: Compute signed and unsigned divider prefixes before mode selection
motivation:
The champion scores 181.38 iterations/s at 76.245 MHz median Gowin
Fmax and 4203513 bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh reproduction matches
its 74.978/76.245 MHz placement-option-0/1 results. Option 1 is limited
by the registered ALU operation code feeding divider remainder launch
state. The existing launch puts mode decoding and signed normalization
before four dependent restoring steps. LESSONS.md and the r6s1/r7s1
histories identify this launch bottleneck, but their remedies also
changed multiply scheduling. Address only prefix preparation here.
Earlier micro_opt result-mux flattening regressed; multiplier latency,
prediction and recurrence changes are outside this hypothesis.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 181.38 iterations/s at 76.245 MHz median Gowin
Fmax and 4203513 bracketed CoreMark cycles. A fresh reproduction matches
its 74.978/76.245 MHz placement-option-0/1 results. Option 1 is limited
by the registered ALU operation code feeding divider remainder launch
state. The existing launch puts mode decoding and signed normalization
before four dependent restoring steps. LESSONS.md and the r6s1/r7s1

Earlier micro_opt result-mux flattening regressed; multiplier latency,
prediction and recurrence changes are outside this hypothesis.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the real divider's four-bit launch prefix with two parallel,
constant combinational arithmetic networks: an unsigned prefix and a
signed-magnitude prefix. Select their completed eight-bit outputs with
the existing signed_op decode. The mode decode must enter only this
final prefix selector, rather than magnitude preparation or either
prefix calculation. This is one local divider-launch micro-optimization;
it adds no state, execution cycle, or new instruction scheduling rule.

For the unsigned path use Nu=m_a[31:28], Du=m_b[3:0], and
small_u=(m_b[31:4]==0 && m_b[3:0]!=0). For the signed path compute
Ns=m_a[31] ? low4((~m_a[31:28])+(m_a[27:0]==0)) : m_a[31:28],
and Ds=m_b[31] ? low4(0-m_b[3:0]) : m_b[3:0]. Compute
small_s=(m_b[3:0]!=0) && (m_b[31] ? m_b[31:4]==28'hfffffff :
m_b[31:4]==0). These signed-path expressions depend on operand sign
bits, never on op or signed_op. The lower-28-bit zero reduction gives
the carry into the leading nibble of a two's-complement magnitude.
This handles INT_MIN without a full-width negation in the prefix path.

For each path implement the complete function F(D,N) returning the
four-bit remainder followed by the four-bit quotient of N divided by D.
For D=0 define F(0,N)={N,4'b0}; for D=1..15 emit literal constants for
{N modulo D, floor(N/D)}. Implement this as logic, not a 256-word ROM:
for each fixed divisor d and each of the eight output bits, form a
16-bit constant truth vector indexed by N. Mask that eight-bit candidate
with D==d, then OR all sixteen candidates. A static generate or explicit
blocks are suitable; each truth-vector lookup has only four inputs.
Do not infer runtime / or %, a synchronous lookup, or a new block RAM.
Use the complete function, without X-valued entries or approximation.

Compute Pu=small_u ? F(Du,Nu) : {Nu,4'b0}, and
Ps=small_s ? F(Ds,Ns) : {Ns,4'b0}. Then prefix_pair is
signed_op ? Ps : Pu, retaining the existing exact signed_op expression
(op==ALU_DIV || op==ALU_REM). The raw-small-divisor guards are essential:
large divisors whose low nibble aliases a small divisor must bypass F.
On accepted launch initialize quotient_q to
{dividend_magnitude[27:0],prefix_pair[3:0]} and remainder_q to
{28'b0,prefix_pair[7:4]}. This must exactly match the current launch
state for every supported DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU operand pair.

Keep full-width dividend/divisor normalization for all other consumers,
all registered unsigned 36-bit divisor multiples, the parallel radix-16
recurrence, seven busy cycles, registered completion, earliest t8 result
consumption, sign restoration and exceptional results unchanged. Keep
reset cancellation, sticky completion, operand snapshots and backpressure.
Preserve every integer and multiply operation, direct registered M inputs,
ALTOPS expressions and schedule, forwarding, predictor, memory handshakes,
nret=1, top-level ports, decoder legality, RVFI ordering and all checks.
Only alu.sv and focused arithmetic tests need implementation changes.

The mechanism is removal of signed-mode decoding and a serial restoring
prefix from the launch arithmetic. Duplicate small prefix logic costs
LUTs but avoids replicating wide arithmetic. A preliminary single-path
logic-map probe reached 77.982 MHz, only 2.28 percent above the champion
and below the acceptance threshold. Its operation decode still preceded
the map. The proposed two-path version moves that selection after both
calculations; the preliminary result does not establish its gain.
Other probes showed that a monolithic constant case inferred a block RAM
and regressed, while retaining serial prefix arithmetic also regressed.
Use four-input truth vectors and explicit divisor masks as specified.

Predict six-percent higher fitness with low confidence pending the full
probe. The recurrence and integer-result forwarding are close competing
timing paths, and duplicate logic or routing can erase the benefit.
Acceptance requires strictly more than 189.72348 iterations/s, roughly
79.751 MHz median Fmax at 4203513 cycles. Use all three vendor placement
options and measured marker-delimited cycles; an isolated improved path
or a single favorable placement is insufficient.

Retain all current real-arithmetic and ALTOPS tests. Exhaust all 256
narrow numerator/divisor pairs, signed carry boundaries with lower 28
bits zero and nonzero, signed and unsigned +/-1..17 divisors, zero,
INT_MIN, UINT_MAX, and large-divisor low-nibble aliases. Check exact
post-acceptance quotient/remainder state as well as final results.
Change live operands and op after acceptance to check snapshot isolation;
check seven iterations, t8 consumption, sticky completion and reset.
Run unchanged pipeline, formal and RVFI cosimulation checks and canonical
CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation under both bus-stall streams.
Normal ALTOPS formal does not prove the real prefix arithmetic.

Retain all checks and add exhaustive narrow-prefix state coverage,

title: Decouple fetch with a fixed-head elastic instruction queue
motivation:
The current champion reaches 181.38 iterations/s at 76.245 MHz and
4203513 marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. Its combinational IF/ID path
advances the fetch PC only when ID advances, so every load-use bubble,
divider wait and older data-memory stall wastes an opportunity to
capture an instruction from the independently stalled instruction bus.
Both buses are unavailable about 22 percent of cycles. Buffered fetch
can overlap those independent delays without changing execution width.

LESSONS.md and the structural entries in experiments/log.jsonl show
that moving forwarding before ID/EX and separating validity from
recovery helped, whereas the r6s1 and r7s1 multiplier pipelines exposed
other arithmetic limits and added cycles. The present proposal keeps
those proven operand boundaries and attacks the pipeline's lockstep
fetch/issue coupling. No prior structural entry tested fetch buffering.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert a four-entry fall-through instruction FIFO inside if_stage.sv,
separating speculative fetch acceptance from ID instruction acceptance.
This is one structural change: make the existing front end elastic.
Keep single issue, nret=1, the current 16-entry agree predictor, early
JAL, integer/multiply arithmetic and the t8 radix-16 divider unchanged.

Each FIFO entry carries the fetched instruction, its own PC and the
predicted_taken bit used to choose that fetch's successor. The fetch
PC addresses the next unbuffered instruction; it is no longer also the
decode PC. On an accepted instruction-bus response, advance this PC
using the existing predictor. Capture responses only with imemReady
asserted and available queue capacity. Holding the address while full
must not enqueue duplicate responses. Prediction and training retain
their existing algorithms, reset state and EX-advancement qualification.

When empty, expose the current raw response directly to ID. If ID can
consume it, advance fetch with no enqueue and no added issue latency.
If ID is held and the response is ready, enqueue it and advance fetch.
When nonempty, expose only the oldest saved entry and assert output
valid independently of imemReady. Pop exactly when ID accepts that
entry; concurrently enqueue a newly accepted response when space is
available. Use four explicit flop entries with a fixed head at index
zero, shifting retained entries toward the head only on consumption.
A simultaneous push writes index old_count - pop, with push taking
priority over shift at that entry. Force syn_ramstyle="registers";
avoid a circular-array read-pointer mux on the decode path. Capacity
and acceptance logic must have no combinational ready/valid loop.
A full queue may conservatively resume filling on the following cycle
after a pop, avoiding a long ID-accept-to-fetch-address enable path.
The measured implementation uses fetch_accept = imem_ready && count!=4,
pop = count!=0 && !stall, and push = fetch_accept && (count!=0 || stall).
The existing stall input becomes the decode-consumption hold. With
the existing if_id_t array, output is the fixed head when count!=0;
otherwise output is the unchanged raw fetch bundle. Clear occupancy
on reset or redirect; payload writes may remain independent of redirect
because a flushed entry is invalid. Keep this validity/payload split.

Rewire hazard handling to test the selected decode instruction and its
availability, rather than raw io_imemData or raw io_imemReady. A load
dependency holds the queue head and injects the existing ID/EX bubble;
backend_hold retains ID/EX but permits independent fetch filling.
An instruction-bus stall injects a decode bubble only when the FIFO is
empty. Preserve conservative source-field comparisons, youngest-writer
forwarding priority, fully forwarded operand capture, and x0 behavior.
ID consumption is selected-entry-valid && !backend_hold && !load_use

title: Isolate branch-predictor resolution from EX forwarding eligibility
motivation:
The champion's sixteen-entry agree predictor already approaches the larger
BHT's measured cycle count: 4203513 versus 4201709. More direction capacity
therefore offers little headroom. A fresh unmodified Gowin placement-0 run
reproduced 74.978 MHz and exposed a more specific predictor integration
problem: the worst path runs from registered rs2 through branch-comparison
carry cells, shared cells named train_next, ctrl_with_trap.reg_write and
rs2_resolved, back to ID/EX. Arrival is 18.632 ns. This is not feedback
through counter state: synthesis shares branch-condition logic between
training and the taken-branch alignment trap that gates forwarding.

Conditional branches never produce a GPR result. Their resolved direction
and target-alignment fault therefore need not participate in EX forwarding
eligibility. Specializing that eligibility by instruction class can remove
the long branch-comparison dependency while preserving the working predictor.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the current sixteen-entry agree predictor, early JAL, training timing,
saved-direction recovery and all pipeline cadence. Isolate predictor/branch
resolution from the EX-to-ID producer-valid path by deriving fwd_w_en from
instruction class and link-write eligibility, rather than the common
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write expression. This is a single branch-resolution
integration change, not a different prediction policy or arithmetic unit.

In ex_stage use the equivalent reachable-state producer predicate:
in.valid && in.ctrl.reg_write && !in.ctrl.is_branch && !misalign_jump &&
!in.ctrl.mem_read && (!is_divide || div_result_valid).
Conditional branches are categorically non-producers before their outcome
is resolved. JAL/JALR remain producers only when their target is aligned;
misaligned jumps must not forward PC+4 or write their link register. Loads
still cannot forward an address as data, and divides become producers only
on valid completion. Preserve x0 filtering and youngest-producer priority
in forward_unit. Illegal instruction controls remain decoder-default inert.

Keep ctrl_with_trap, misalign_fault, architectural EX/MEM.pc_next, reg_write
at EX/MEM, branch comparison, redirect and train_valid/train_agree unchanged.
In particular do not globally remove branch alignment faults or change the
registered trap-adjusted write controls. The only disconnected dependency
is taken-branch alignment resolution into the combinational EX forwarding
predicate. RVFI traps, sequential trap fallback, actual successor and link
write suppression remain exactly as before. No speculative result, predictor
update queue, target cache, additional stage or recovery bubble is introduced.

Verify the producer predicate is equivalent to the original for every
reachable legal/illegal decoded instruction, including all six branch
conditions and taken/not-taken aligned/misaligned targets. The proof relies
on the enforced decoder property is_branch implies !reg_write. Do not
assume arbitrary inconsistent control bundles are architectural inputs;
assert that decoder property explicitly instead of weakening trap checks.
Exercise adjacent consumers whose raw source numbers alias branch encoding
rd bits, so an incorrect branch producer would corrupt forwarded operands.

The hypothesis is a timing opportunity, with expected unchanged 4203513
CoreMark cycles. Predict five percent higher fitness with LOW confidence:
the divider feedback path is nearly tied with the current worst path, and
placement can dominate. A broader isolated probe that changed the global
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write expression passed all 30 existing pipeline tests
but fell to 73.778 MHz in placement 0. That probe is not the proposed change;
keep the registered trap controls intact and specialize only fwd_w_en.
Other probes of registered recovery and altered predictor state also lost
first-placement Fmax, so none of those changes belongs in this hypothesis.

No measured fitness improvement is claimed. At 4203513 marker-delimited

progress bound, and real/ALTOPS M arithmetic. Run unchanged formal, pipeline
and decoder tests, cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART validation.

title: Shorten integer ALU carry propagation with block carry select
motivation:
The champion scores 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz with 3978988
marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path begins at
ID/EX is_auipc and traverses EX, the ALU and forwarding into ID operand
capture. The remaining ordinary integer arithmetic is on a feedback
path used by dependent instructions. Earlier micro_opt result-mux
flattening regressed, while divider-prefix duplication gained only
0.17 percent. Target carry propagation in integer ADD/SUB instead of
repeating those changes or adding instruction latency.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz with 3978988
marker-delimited CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path begins at
ID/EX is_auipc and traverses EX, the ALU and forwarding into ID operand
capture. The remaining ordinary integer arithmetic is on a feedback
path used by dependent instructions. Earlier micro_opt result-mux

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the combinational ALU_ADD and ALU_SUB arithmetic networks
with explicit four-block, eight-bit carry-select adders. Compute each
block's sums for carry-in zero and one independently. Derive each block's
generate bit from its zero-carry sum and its propagate bit from the
reduction AND of operand XOR. Compute the four block-boundary carries
with parallel lookahead equations, then select each output byte with
that block's carry. Do not ripple carry through four result muxes.
ADD uses a, b and initial carry zero. SUB uses a, bitwise-not b and
initial carry one. Keep ADD and SUB networks separate so operation
decoding does not enter a shared operand-inversion or carry-in path.
All arithmetic is modulo 2^32; discard only the final carry.

Use portable synthesizable SystemVerilog with statically sized
expressions. Prefer a local combinational function in alu.sv, with
explicit widths for nine-bit speculative sums and eight-bit results.
Keep the existing ALU case selection, immediate/AUIPC operand routing,
shifts, comparisons, multiplication and every divider path unchanged.
No extra register, pipeline stage, bypass rule, instruction scheduling
change, predictor change or memory change is part of this hypothesis.
Preserve fully forwarded ID/EX operands, valid-qualified side effects,
bus holds, nret=1 ports, decoder legality, RVFI and retirement ordering.
Retain the exact M-extension ALTOPS formulas and real-arithmetic branch.

The intended benefit is a shorter ordinary-ALU-to-ID operand feedback
path, improving Fmax without changing CoreMark cycles. Extra speculative
adders and selection routing cost LUTs; Gowin may remap the logic into
a long carry chain, or the divider and multiply paths may cap the gain.
The eight-percent gain is an unmeasured estimate with low confidence.
Inspect vendor timing and compare all three placement options; a lower
source-level logic depth alone is insufficient. Acceptance requires
fitness strictly above 200.06842 iterations/s, approximately 79.607 MHz
at the champion's cycle count.

Keep every existing test and gate. Add exact ADD/SUB vectors that
propagate carry or borrow across every eight-bit boundary and across
all 32 bits, including zero, UINT_MAX, INT_MIN, signed overflow and
deterministic random operands. Exercise dependent ALU chains, AUIPC,
immediate address calculations and held operands through bus stalls.
Run ALU/pipeline suites, unchanged formal and RVFI cosimulation, and
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks with both stall streams.
Marker-delimited cycles should remain exactly 3978988; investigate any
change. No timing improvement is claimed measured at proposal time.

title: Replace divider launch-prefix work with seven uniform radix-32 iterations
motivation:
The current champion scores 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz and
3978988 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior structural successes removed
serial divider depth and registered its completion; r6s1/r7s1 multiplier
pipelines instead exposed divider launch/recurrence limits. The current
launch edge normalizes operands, builds divisor multiples, and performs
four serial narrow restoring steps. The r8s0 prefix-only rewrite reached
76.371 MHz and did not clear acceptance. Change the divider's work
schedule so launch does no quotient selection, retaining the proven
registered completion and unchanged t8 acceptance time.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current champion scores 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz and
3978988 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior structural successes removed
serial divider depth and registered its completion; r6s1/r7s1 multiplier
pipelines instead exposed divider launch/recurrence limits. The current
launch edge normalizes operands, builds divisor multiples, and performs
four serial narrow restoring steps. The r8s0 prefix-only rewrite reached
76.371 MHz and did not clear acceptance. Change the divider's work
schedule so launch does no quotient selection, retaining the proven
registered completion and unchanged t8 acceptance time.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the launch-prefix plus seven radix-16 iterations with launch
normalization plus seven uniform radix-32 iterations. This is one
structural redesign of the divider's digit width and register boundaries.
Retain the existing request/busy/done controller, seven busy edges,
earliest t8 result handshake and sticky completion. Keep the integer
pipeline, combinational multiplication, forwarding, four-entry elastic
fetch queue, predictor and all memory/retirement interfaces unchanged.

On accepted launch capture the original dividend, signedness, quotient
and remainder signs, desired result kind, zero-divisor flag and normalized
unsigned divisor. Initialize a 35-bit quotient register to the 32-bit
unsigned dividend magnitude with three leading zero bits; initialize the
32-bit remainder to zero. Remove small_divisor qualification and every
prefix quotient/remainder calculation. Preserve full-width normalization,
including the magnitude of INT_MIN, and request-time operand snapshots.

Capture widened divisor multiples 1D through 31D at launch in a full
registered bank. Use 37 unsigned bits throughout: 31*UINT_MAX fits and
all five incoming bits participate in each borrow decision. Reuse the
normalized divisor register for 1D. Generate each constant product from
at most three signed power-of-two terms with explicitly widened shifts,
adds and subtracts, registering the full product independently. Use a
canonical signed-digit expansion: repeatedly choose digit 2-(k modulo 4)
for an odd k, subtract that digit, then shift k right; this yields terms
0,+1,-1. Form the positive terms first, then subtract negative terms.
Examples are 3D=4D-D, 11D=16D-D-4D, 13D=16D+D-4D,
19D=16D+4D-D, 21D=16D+4D+D, 23D=32D-D-8D,
25D=32D+D-8D, 27D=32D-D-4D, 29D=32D-D-2D and 31D=32D-D.
Keep all intermediates 37 bits, so the exact arithmetic is retained.
Do not explicitly replace the even-product registers with shifts of odd
registers: that area-saving probe regressed to 68.083 MHz. Do not use
carry-save constant-product logic: that probe regressed to 74.762 MHz.
Preserve the direct full-bank capture topology and the existing request
enable. No runtime division, modulo, ROM, vendor primitive or extra cycle.

At each of seven busy edges form T={remainder_q,quotient_q[34:30]}.
Compute all 31 independent widened subtractions {0,T}-{0,kD} in
38 bits. success[k] is the inverse borrow bit. Select digit zero when
success[1] is false, digit k for success[k] && !success[k+1], and digit
31 when success[31] is true. Form 32 mutually exclusive 37-bit candidates
containing {selected_remainder[31:0],digit[4:0]} and combine them with an
explicit balanced 32-to-16-to-8-to-4-to-2-to-1 masked-OR tree. Capture
quotient_q={quotient_q[29:0],digit} and remainder_q=selected_remainder.
For nonzero D, R<D implies T<32D, making each selected digit exact and
the new remainder fit 32 bits. Starting with three leading zeros means
seven five-bit shifts process precisely the 32 dividend bits; the first
digit consumes only two nonzero-capable source bits. The final quotient
is quotient_q[31:0], with its upper three bits zero for nonzero divisors.

Only completed quotient/remainder registers feed the existing sign and
zero-divisor correction. Preserve all-ones DIV/DIVU by zero, original
bit-pattern REM/REMU by zero, INT_MIN/-1 quotient and zero remainder,
signed truncation and remainder sign. Zero-divisor recurrence may select
31, but the registered architectural override remains authoritative.
Keep real and ALTOPS request/wait/result timing identical, retaining every
existing ALTOPS XOR formula. Reset cancels pending work; completion freezes
until consumed; never forward an intermediate quotient or replay a divide.

A temporary radix-32 probe with this canonical shift/add/subtract bank
passed lint, the existing pipeline suite, selftest RVFI comparison with
ready and stalled buses, and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/
marker validation. CoreMark retained exactly 3978988 timed cycles.
Gowin placements 0/1/2 measured 77.405/78.538/78.538 MHz, using 6598 LUTs,
2733 registers, zero LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs. This implies
197.382 iterations/s, approximately 3.2 percent higher fitness, below
acceptance. The carry-save, odd-sharing and alternative additive bank probes
passed the adapted real/ALTOPS arithmetic suites. The additive bank
reached only 76.446 MHz; retain the specified canonical formulation.
Formal has not been run.

Predict three percent higher fitness with low confidence. This is the
best measured structural direction in this proposal session, but it has
not demonstrated the required tournament margin. The wider bank and
32-way selection increase routing/fanout, and ordinary EX feedback now
competes with divider launch/recurrence for the critical path. Acceptance
requires strictly more than 200.06842 iterations/s, or 79.606984 MHz median
Fmax at unchanged cycles. Measure all three placements and the actual
marker-delimited cycles. Preserve nret=1, core ports, every hard invariant
and all evaluation files. Run unchanged formal and RVFI cosimulation gates;
ALTOPS formal alone does not establish the new real arithmetic.

Adapt internal arithmetic-state assertions to a 35-bit initial quotient,
zero initial remainder and five-bit recurrence without removing any
existing operand vector or architectural assertion. Extend the existing
arbitrary-R<D recurrence test from 16 to all 32 digit possibilities,
check all 31 registered multiples, boundaries kD-1/kD/kD+1, maximum
37-bit trials, and large divisors. Retain signed/unsigned corner cases,
zero division, input changes after launch, seven busy edges, t8 acceptance,
long completion backpressure, reset cancellation and all pipeline hazards.

title: Balance the branch-condition tree feeding predictor recovery and training
motivation:
The existing agree predictor and early JAL already remove most direct
control-flow bubbles. A reference CoreMark profile counted 529588
conditional branches and only 13735 returns in the measured interval;
a return stack therefore offers little throughput headroom. The prior
r8s2 timing investigation identified the branch comparison feeding
predictor training and trap-qualified forwarding as a long path, but
changing forwarding eligibility regressed. The opportunity is to shorten
the predictor's outcome-resolution network while retaining its policy,
recovery timing and all trap-adjusted producer semantics.

title: Register ALU operation decode alongside execution operands
motivation: The champion reaches 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz. Its timing limits include ordinary ALU-to-ID feedback and divider launch. Several local timing probes exposed registered alu_op decoding ahead of divider normalization or result selection. Earlier r4s0 flattened ALU result selection but left operation decoding in EX and regressed; r9s0 carry-select arithmetic also regressed. Move the operation decoder across the existing ID/EX boundary while preserving the arithmetic and execution schedule.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a nineteen-bit alu_select payload to id_ex_t. In ID compute alu_select[k] = (dec_alu_op == k) for k=0..18 and capture it with the existing operand/control payload enable. Reset this vector to zero with the bundle; hold it through backend and load-use holds. Keep the existing five-bit alu_op for execution classification, divider result-kind capture and ALTOPS operation dispatch. There is no new pipeline stage or instruction latency. Operation selection is decoded from the validated current instruction and travels with its fully forwarded operands, never from the subsequent live fetch.

Pass alu_select from EX into the internal ALU module. Use its registered bits directly as the mutually exclusive result enables for ADD, SUB, bitwise operations, SLT/SLTU, shifts, LUI and the four multiply operations. Implement parallel masked candidates and a balanced bitwise OR, with no priority chain or re-encoding back to an operation number. Bits 15..18 correspond to DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU, so their combinational out remains zero. An all-zero vector also produces zero. For the real divider launch use alu_select[ALU_DIV] | alu_select[ALU_REM] as signed_op, replacing the five-bit equality decoders ahead of magnitude conversion and the launch prefix. Retain the full current signed-magnitude, prefix, divisor-multiple, recurrence and sign/exception arithmetic exactly. This is a single operation-decode retiming micro-optimization; the result mux consumes the predecoded representation directly.

Keep every arithmetic operator and operand source unchanged, including direct registered m_a/m_b, separate existing multiplication expressions, integer a/b selection and exact ALTOPS constants. The ALTOPS combinational multiply candidates use the same registered selects as the real branch. Division ALTOPS dispatch and request/completion timing stay unchanged. Preserve seven busy edges, registered completion, earliest t8 acceptance, held results and reset cancellation. No speculative arithmetic result may forward before valid completion.

Preserve the existing EX forwarding eligibility, EX/MEM result selection, branch alignment/trap logic, predictor training/recovery, fetch FIFO, register-file storage and WB bypass, memory handshakes, nret=1 interface and RVFI ordering. Raw instruction handling and payload enables remain independent of redirect; validity still controls effects. This is not a predictor-policy, carry-network or multiplier-sharing change. No synthesis keep attributes or vendor primitives are required.

The intended gain is removal of EX operation-decode delay and fanout ahead of divider normalization and ALU selection. Extra control registers and mask routing can offset that benefit, and synthesis can recreate a priority network unless the mutually exclusive parallel topology is explicit. Predict six percent higher fitness with low confidence; no measured improvement is established. A preliminary registered-select probe using a reverse case statement passed all 33 existing pipeline tests but measured 55.889/59.056/59.056 MHz across placements 0/1/2, a substantial regression. That case-based probe does not establish a gain for the proposed parallel selection; eliminating its priority topology is essential, and the negative result warrants low confidence. The final specified parallel masked-OR implementation has not been timed or formally checked. Other isolated probes in this session, including bypass one-hot selection, shared multiplication, register-file one-hot reads, writeback selection retiming and a lone registered divider-mode bit, failed to beat the champion and are excluded from this proposal. The single mode-bit probe's 71.608 MHz motivates evaluating the complete decode relocation, not claiming that the isolated change helped.

Adapt standalone ALU drivers to provide the matching vector, retaining every existing operand, expected result and handshake assertion. Exercise all 32 operation encodings, zero select, all integer shift amounts and signed comparisons, signed/unsigned multiply halves, division sign/zero/overflow cases and changes to live inputs after request acceptance. In the pipeline test back-to-back different ALU classes, forwarded dependencies, loads, jumps, branch recovery, divide completion, backend holds and reset; verify selection and operands remain associated.

Run the unchanged formal and RVFI cosimulation gates, real and ALTOPS arithmetic suites, and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation with both bus stalls. The cycle schedule should retain exactly 3978988 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 200.06842 iterations/s, equivalent to median Gowin Fmax above 79.607 MHz at that count. Measure all three placement options and inspect the resulting paths. motivation:
The champion scores 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz and 3978988 timed

boundaries around forwarding and division. Registered multiplication
(r6s1/r7s1) exposed divider timing limits and added dependency bubbles;

Fmax when they changed operand storage or delayed forwarding. Instead,

ALU result selection and divider launch currently decode a registered
five-bit operation before driving wide datapaths.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Capture a decoded execution descriptor with every ID/EX entry: fifteen
one-hot ordinary-ALU/MUL result enables, a signed-division flag and a
remainder-selection flag. This is one structural retiming of execution
control. Keep the existing operand registers, forwarding topology,
instruction-stage count, arithmetic circuits and operation latencies.

In ID compute alu_select = 15'b1 << dec_alu_op, where bits 0..14 map
exactly to ALU_ADD through ALU_MULHSU in core_pkg.sv. DIV/REM operations
15..18 yield an all-zero ordinary-result mask. Compute divide_signed
for ALU_DIV/ALU_REM and divide_remainder for ALU_REM/ALU_REMU. Capture all
three fields inside the existing ID/EX payload update, alongside alu_op;
reset clears them, backend_hold/load_use retain them, and redirect acts
only on validity. Keep alu_op for the existing execute-class detection
and exact ALTOPS division formulas. Do not introduce a second instruction
decoder or relax the original default-illegal validation.

Feed these registered controls into the ALU. Replace its combinational
op-to-result case decode with fifteen mutually exclusive masked result
candidates and an OR reduction. Every candidate computes exactly the
current expression: ADD/SUB, logical operations, signed/unsigned compare,
all shifts, LUI, and the four current multiply results. Compute the
arithmetic in parallel, mask each 32-bit result with its registered
one-hot bit, then combine with a balanced OR tree. All-zero selection
returns zero as before. Do not implement a priority case over the one-hot
bits, add syn_keep constraints, share/replace arithmetic, or change the
three existing real multiply expressions. The important difference from
r4s0's unsuccessful local result-mux rewrite is that operation decoding
now precedes the register boundary rather than remaining in EX.

Use the registered divide_signed flag instead of decoding op in the
real divider's signed_op path; use divide_remainder when capturing
want_remainder_q. Keep full-width normalization, the narrow launch
prefix, all registered divisor multiples, seven busy iterations, earliest
t8 transfer, sign correction, zero-divisor override, sticky completion
and reset cancellation unchanged. Operands remain the original direct
registered m_a/m_b sources. Preserve the encoded-op DIV/REM ALTOPS case
and its exact formulas behind the unchanged controller. For the four
multiply result candidates, select the existing ALTOPS formulas under
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS and real products otherwise.

The expected benefit is removing post-register opcode decoding from
ordinary result selection and divider normalization/prefix launch, while

stalls or forwarding sources are introduced. The decoder-to-ID/EX path
gets wider, and the registered one-hot controls add routing/fanout; the
remaining branch, multiplier and divider paths can erase the benefit.

title: Predecode branch comparison classes before the predictor resolution stage
motivation: The current sixteen-entry agree predictor already captures most direct-control cycle savings. Previous r8s2 forwarding specialization and r9s2 comparator balancing regressed. Both retained a binary branch_op field decoded again in EX, where selection, branch outcome, predictor recovery and trap-qualified forwarding form a feedback path to ID. Move only the branch-condition selection decode before ID/EX, using registered one-hot comparison classes while retaining the original word-wide comparison operators and predictor policy.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a three-bit branch_class and a branch_invert bit to ctrl_t, captured with the existing decoded controls in ID/EX. Decode dec_branch_op in ID as follows: BEQ/BNE select class 001 (equality), BLT/BGE select 010 (signed less-than), BLTU/BGEU select 100 (unsigned less-than). Set branch_invert for BNE, BGE and BGEU. For reserved comparison encodings select 000 and clear branch_invert. Derive these controls from the validated decoder outputs, independent of readiness, redirect, producer selection and branch outcome. Preserve decoder default-illegal behavior. Existing branch_op may remain for interface/test compatibility; synthesis may prune its unused registered copy.

In EX retain three ordinary word-wide comparison expressions: eq=(rs1==rs2), slt=($signed(rs1)<$signed(rs2)), and ult=(rs1<rs2), using the current fully forwarded, registered source operands. Replace only the six-way binary branch_op case selection with branch_cond=((in.ctrl.branch_class[0] && eq) || (in.ctrl.branch_class[1] && slt) || (in.ctrl.branch_class[2] && ult)) ^ in.ctrl.branch_invert. The registered classes are one-hot or zero. With zero class the inversion bit must be zero. Equality for BGE/BGEU is handled by inversion of strict less-than. Do not introduce a nibble/byte comparison tree, an operand-sign bias network, speculative history, or an additional pipeline stage.

The architectural change is moving instruction-class selection across the existing ID/EX boundary. title: Isolate the divider launch nibble from full-width dividend negation
motivation: The champion scores 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz with 3978988 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent micro_opt operation-decode changes regressed, and timing repeatedly exposed magnitude preparation followed by the four-bit launch prefix. Prior lookup-prefix duplication gained only 0.17 percent. Compute only the leading dividend magnitude nibble with a small exact Boolean network, leaving the existing prefix arithmetic, divisor normalization and divider schedule intact.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz with 3978988 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent micro_opt operation-decode changes regressed, and timing repeatedly exposed magnitude preparation followed by the four-bit launch prefix. Prior lookup-prefix duplication gained only 0.17 percent. Compute only the leading dividend magnitude nibble with a small exact Boolean network, leaving the existing prefix arithmetic, divisor normalization and divider schedule intact.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the dependency of the real divider's launch-prefix input on a full-width dividend negation with a dedicated four-bit magnitude calculation. Let n=signed_op && m_a[31] and z=OR(m_a[27:0]). Compute prefix[0]=m_a[28] XOR (n AND z). For k=1..3 compute prefix[k]=m_a[28+k] XOR (n AND (z OR OR(m_a[27+k:28]))). Use constant slices and a shared balanced lower-28-bit OR reduction. This is the exact identity (-x)[i]=x[i] XOR OR(x[i-1:0]) when negating, specialized to bits 31:28. It handles the carry boundary when all lower 28 bits are zero, including zero and INT_MIN, without propagating a carry from bit zero into the launch nibble.

Feed this prefix directly to prefix_quotient[0] and to the large-divisor remainder initialization currently using dividend_magnitude[31:28]. Retain ordinary conditional negation for the lower 28 dividend bits used by quotient_q initialization; it can be expressed at 28-bit width and concatenated with prefix, using the original n derived from bit 31, never bit 27. This is bit-for-bit equivalent to the original full magnitude. Leave divisor_magnitude, its small-divisor guard, all four serial narrow restoring-prefix steps and every registered divisor multiple exactly unchanged. Do not replace the whole dividend or divisor with a full-width prefix network, duplicate signed/unsigned prefix engines, or change the prefix into a lookup table.

This is one local combinational arithmetic micro-optimization. Preserve the first four quotient bits computed at accepted launch, seven following radix-16 busy cycles, registered completion, earliest t8 result handshake, sticky backpressure, reset cancellation, captured signs, original dividend, zero-divisor override and INT_MIN/-1 results. Leave result sign correction, ordinary ALU and multiply expressions, direct M inputs, all ALTOPS formulas and schedule, forwarding, holds, prediction/FIFO, memory handshakes, decoder legality, nret=1 and every RVFI contract unchanged. No new state, stage, instruction latency, synthesis constraints or keep attributes are required.

The intended gain is removing a wide carry path from the leading-nibble input while adding only one shared reduction and four conditional XOR functions. title: Pipeline M-unit preparation and completion at existing stage boundaries
motivation:
The champion delivers 191.27 iterations/s at 76.107 MHz with 3978988
timed CoreMark cycles. Prior registered-multiply attempts r6s1/r7s1
shortened product delivery but exposed divider launch and recurrence
paths; r7s1 limited multiply-related cycle overhead to 0.85 percent by
forwarding products from MEM instead of globally stalling multiplication.
The r9s1 radix-32 attempt and r10s1 decoded-control attempt regressed:
neither inserted a register between signed normalization and divisor
preparation, nor removed the combinational product-to-ID feedback path.
Address these timing boundaries together as one M-unit pipeline redesign.
A temporary combined probe now reaches 84.715 MHz median Fmax with just
0.128 percent more timed cycles, supporting this specific combination.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give the M-extension a registered preparation/completion topology while
retaining single issue, nret=1, the current integer pipeline, predictor,
four-entry fetch queue, and worst-case divide acceptance at t8. This is
one structural redesign of M execution, not a change to instruction or
memory prediction. Ordinary integer operations keep their existing EX
result and forwarding paths.

For multiplication, capture one signed 66-bit product at the existing
EX/MEM boundary. Use signed 33-bit operands from the fully forwarded
ID/EX rs1_val and rs2_val: sign-extend A only for MULH/MULHSU and B only
for MULH, otherwise zero-extend. Select product[31:0] for MUL and
product[63:32] for high-half operations in MEM, feeding both MEM-to-ID
forwarding and MEM/WB. Carry product selection and validity with its
instruction under exactly the EX/MEM hold/bubble rules. Remove the
combinational multiplier from the active ordinary ALU result and EX
forwarding paths. Independent multiplies can advance every cycle.
Interlock an immediate consumer of a valid legal EX multiply just like
an EX load: one bubble, then capture the MEM product. Never impose a
global multiply wait. Keep youngest-writer priority, x0, source snapshots,
exact-once retirement, and multiply-to-store/branch/divide dependencies.
Keep the hazard module unchanged: in core.sv drive its existing EX-load
input with id_ex_w.ctrl.mem_read || ex_multiply. EX exports ex_multiply
qualified by valid, legal and ALU_MUL<=alu_op<=ALU_MULHSU. Existing
backend-hold priority and conservative raw source comparisons then apply.

Retiming the divider is necessary to avoid merely exposing the launch
path seen in prior multiplier attempts. On request edge t0, capture
normalized 32-bit unsigned magnitudes A and D, original dividend, zero
divisor flag, quotient/remainder signs and result-kind selection. No
quotient-digit work or divisor-multiple addition follows normalization
before this register. Inputs after t0 cannot affect the operation.

On preparation edge t1, independently capture widened multiples k*D for
k=2..31 in 37-bit registers from registered D; reuse the zero-extended
divisor register itself for 1D. Express each constant product with its
canonical signed-digit expansion: repeatedly choose digit 2-(k modulo 4)
for odd k, subtract that digit, then shift k right. Sum positive shifted
terms in ascending shift order, then subtract negative shifted terms in
ascending order, with every intermediate 37 bits. For example 11D is
(D<<4)-D-(D<<2), 13D is D+(D<<4)-(D<<2), and 31D is (D<<5)-D.
These are elaboration-time constants, not runtime multiply, division or
modulo. Generate each multiple directly, with a common t1 bank enable,
rather than chaining registers or sharing shifted odd-product registers.
Preserve the full borrow width and do not add synthesis keep attributes.
On the same t1 edge process only A[31:30], a two-bit prefix. For nonzero
D<=3, use two narrow restoring steps to produce two-bit Q2 and R2;
otherwise Q2=0 and R2=A[31:30]. Initialize 32-bit quotient_q to
{A[29:0],Q2} and remainder_q to zero-extended R2. Test D<=3 using all
upper divisor bits so large-divisor aliases never enter this prefix.
For D=0 the registered architectural result override is authoritative.

At edges t2 through t7 perform six radix-32 iterations. Form the
37-bit trial T={remainder_q,quotient_q[31:27]}. Compute 31 independent
38-bit subtractions {0,T}-{0,kD}. The inverse high borrow bit is
success[k]. Choose digit zero if !success[1], digit k when success[k]
&& !success[k+1], or digit 31 when success[31]. Use mutually exclusive
masked candidates and an explicit balanced 32-way OR tree to select
{remainder[31:0],digit[4:0]}. Capture quotient_q as
{quotient_q[26:0],digit}, and the new remainder. For D!=0, R<D implies
T<32D; the selected remainder therefore fits 32 bits. The two-bit prefix
plus six five-bit digits process exactly 32 dividend bits.

Set sticky completion after t7 and allow EX/MEM transfer at t8, exactly
matching the current external divider schedule. Restore signs only from
the completed state. Preserve DIV/DIVU by zero, REM/REMU by zero,
INT_MIN/-1, signed truncation and remainder sign. An older dmem stall
may overlap all preparation/iteration work and must retain completion
until accepted. Drain older EX/MEM entries once, then inject invalid
bubbles while division waits. Reset cancels every pending operation.
Do not add a ninth divider wait cycle or shorten the formal-only timing.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS preserve all existing exact formulas. Capture
multiply substitutes at the same product boundary and deliver them from
MEM with identical dependency latency. Keep division substitutes behind
the same t0/t1/t2..t7/t8 controller as real division. Preserve the decoder's
default-illegal behavior, alignment traps, validity-only recovery, all
core ports, single-channel RVFI order and every evaluation invariant.

The intended improvement is that no clock period contains both signed
normalization and wide multiple preparation, or both an unregistered
multiply and the ID forwarding mux. Unlike r9s1, radix 32 buys a separate
preparation cycle rather than seven uniform digits at unchanged launch
depth. Unlike r7s1, divider launch has a real register boundary instead
of a combinational prefix rewrite. The larger subtractor bank and
routing, or ordinary integer/branch feedback, may become limiting.
A temporary implementation passed Verilator lint and all eight full RVFI
comparisons for selftest/random1/random2/random3, with ready buses and
with both stall streams. Canonical CoreMark passed CRC, success-text,
bounded-access and timing-marker validation in 3984075 measured cycles,
only 5087 cycles (0.128 percent) above the champion. Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 gave 77.651/84.715/84.715 MHz, a median of 84.715 MHz,
using 6597 LUTs, 2791 registers, no LUT-RAM, four BSRAMs and two DSPs.
This implies 212.63405 iterations/s, 11.17 percent above 191.27. The
median-placement worst paths are now ordinary EX arithmetic at 17.099 ns
and the divider recurrence at 17.097 ns. The placement spread remains a
risk; these are exploratory measurements, not an accepted evaluation.

The adapted real-arithmetic and ALTOPS suites passed with all original
operand vectors retained. Internal checks model t0 magnitude capture,
t1 prefix/multiples and six subsequent digits; the recurrence test covers
all 32 digits and all 31 multiples. Existing pipeline checks passed after
changing only the immediate-MUL latency expectation to one bubble.
An added pipeline test passed 192 operand pairs across all four multiply
kinds, both with ready buses and randomized stalls plus an older store
held for twelve cycles. It checked exact RVFI operands/results and memory,
consecutive independent product retirements, one dependent-consumer bubble
and x0 handling through the registered product boundary.
Formal and formal-deep have not been run on the probe. Predict eleven
percent higher fitness with medium confidence. The unchanged t8 divide
schedule preserves the current ready-bus progress bound, while dependent
multiplies add cycles. Accept only measured median Gowin Fmax times
marker-delimited throughput strictly above 200.06842 iterations/s, using
all three placement options. At 3984075 cycles this requires more than
79.708759 MHz median Fmax. Repeat all unchanged correctness gates during
implementation; do not infer formal arithmetic correctness from ALTOPS.

Preserve every real-arithmetic test vector, moving multiply checks to
the new registered result interface rather than deleting coverage.
Check every multiply kind and all radix-32 digits, widened multiples,
kD-1/kD/kD+1 boundaries, full-width dividends/divisors, signed extremes,
reset, changed live inputs, preparation timing and completion holds.
Update internal recurrence models without weakening architectural
assertions. Verify one immediate-multiply dependency bubble and no
bubble for independent consecutive multiplies. Run unchanged formal,
RVFI cosimulation with both stall streams, and canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks. ALTOPS does not prove real M arithmetic.

title: Predecode the predicted branch outcome into a registered recovery mask
motivation:
The champion already predicts direct branches and JAL. Recent r9s2 and
r10s2 comparator balancing and comparison-class predecode changed no
CoreMark cycles and lost Fmax. The remaining predictor opportunity is
the late recovery dependency: the current EX path selects an architectural
branch condition, qualifies taken/alignment, then compares against the
saved predicted_taken bit. Prediction is already known in ID, so its
polarity can be folded into registered recovery controls before EX.

A retirement-order profile of the canonical timed region found 2922016
instructions, 529588 conditional branches and only 13735 JALRs. Its
sixteen-entry agree model missed 55124 directions. These are software
profile counts, not cycle-accurate predictor measurements. They argue
against expecting the acceptance margin from a JALR target table alone.
The proposed change targets recovery timing with unchanged prediction
policy and pipeline cadence.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a six-bit branch_recover_mask to id_ex_t. This mask describes which
primitive comparison outcome would contradict the prediction already
attached to the selected IF/ID instruction. Generate it in ID from the
validated branch control, branch_op and in.predicted_taken, independently
of operand values. Keep the existing encoded branch_op and architectural
branch comparator. This is one predictor-resolution retiming: move the
combination of instruction condition and prediction polarity before the
ID/EX register, rather than merely registering comparison classes.

Define mask bits [0..5] as recovery on EQ, NE, signed-LT, signed-GE,
unsigned-LT, unsigned-GE respectively. For a legal conditional branch
predicted not taken, set its natural condition bit: BEQ->0, BNE->1,
BLT->2, BGE->3, BLTU->4, BGEU->5. For the same branch predicted taken,
set the opposite bit within its pair (natural index XOR 1). All other
instructions and reserved branch encodings get mask zero. Exactly one
bit is set for a legal branch. Capture under the existing ID/EX payload
enable, reset to zero, and retain across backend_hold and load_use.
Prediction must come from the selected queue entry, not from the raw
fetch address or the current predictor table. Keep leading PC/operand
fields and trailing instr/predicted_taken/valid placement consistent with
test helpers, inserting the new field before ctrl or instr.

In EX compute the ordinary full-width primitive results eq=(rs1==rs2),
slt=($signed(rs1)<$signed(rs2)), and ult=(rs1<rs2), using the current
registered, fully forwarded operands. Produce raw_branch_mismatch as
(mask[0]&eq) | (mask[1]&!eq) | (mask[2]&slt) |
(mask[3]&!slt) | (mask[4]&ult) | (mask[5]&!ult).
Use a balanced OR of the three two-term condition pairs, not a priority
selection. The registered mask includes prediction polarity, so this
path does not select branch_cond and subsequently XOR predicted_taken.
Do not add syn_keep or duplicate operand registers. The existing
architectural branch_cond case may share these primitive results, but
its behavior, signedness and reserved-selector default remain unchanged.

Handle alignment separately and exactly. Let direct_aligned be
(branch_target[1:0]==0). Define branch_mismatch = direct_aligned ?
raw_branch_mismatch : in.predicted_taken. An unaligned direct target
can never be an effective taken successor under the existing trap
policy, so comparison against the saved direction reduces to that bit.
Use control_advance && in.ctrl.is_branch && branch_mismatch for branch
recovery. Keep the original effective_taken-versus-predicted_taken test
for JAL/JALR and the original unconditional fence_i_advance term. The
same control_advance qualification must prevent updates or recovery from
invalid, illegal, reset or held EX instructions.

Keep branch_taken, misalign_branch, misalign_jump, ctrl_with_trap,
fwd_w_en, branch/jump target adders, redirect_target, train_valid,
train_index, train_agree and EX/MEM.pc_next behavior unchanged. In
particular do not use the recovery mask as architectural branch_taken,
change a misalignment trap, suppress its required link-write blocking,
or repeat the earlier forwarding-eligibility specialization. Saved
direction still selects the direct correction endpoint exactly as today.
EX/MEM.pc_next and RVFI must always describe the resolved successor.

Preserve the sixteen-entry binary agree table, PC[5:2] indexing, weakly
agree reset, pre-edge read/write semantics, early JAL, sequential JALR,
four-entry fixed-head elastic queue and empty bypass. Preserve recovery
priority over unavailable imem, full queue flushing, FENCE.I ordering,
validity-only squashing, payload independence from redirect, all memory
and divide handshakes, arithmetic, decoder legality, nret=1, all external
ports and every hard invariant. No new pipeline stage or recovery bubble
is introduced; expect the champion's 3978988 timed CoreMark cycles.

Predict five percent higher fitness with low confidence. This exact
prediction-conditioned mask has not been implemented or timed. It is
not the r10s2 comparison-class predecode: that variant left prediction
polarity after the selected architectural condition. Exploratory probes
in this session rejected one-hot counters (66.947 MHz in placement 0)
and cached one-hot prediction (62.266 MHz). Moving comparison slices
into ID also failed: the best full-slice probe, eight four-bit groups,
reached 72.338 MHz median with unchanged cycles and valid CoreMark CRCs;
asymmetric low-part retiming reached only 56.099-66.815 MHz in placement
0. None is part of this proposal. They show why operand retiming and
counter recoding should not be bundled into this attempt. The proposed
mask changes only instruction/prediction control preparation in ID.

The risk is that Gowin already folds these Boolean operations, or that
unchanged branch-to-forwarding, divider launch and ALU-to-ID paths dominate.
Added mask registers and fanout can also lower Fmax. Require unchanged
formal, full small-program RVFI cosimulation with both stall modes,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks and all three vendor
placements. Acceptance above 191.27*1.046=200.06842 iterations/second
requires approximately 79.607 MHz median at the expected cycle count.
Do not claim improvement from predicate equivalence or a single placement.

title: Select radix-32 divider results with a balanced threshold mux tree
motivation:
The champion delivers 208.94 iterations/s at 83.245 MHz, with 3984075
measured CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md records that r5s1 improved timing
with parallel divisor subtraction and that r11s1 isolated normalization
and multiplication at existing register boundaries. The current radix-32
recurrence still converts 31 borrow decisions into adjacent-threshold
one-hot selects, gates 32 full candidate payloads, then OR-reduces them.
This adds decode and distribution after the wide subtraction decisions.
Prior micro_opt carry-select, ALU decode and launch-prefix attempts
r9s0/r10s0/r11s0 did not improve these recurrence selection paths.
Exploratory timing identifies divider recurrence paths very close to
ordinary EX feedback. Rewriting only the local selection topology can
reduce this logic and its routing burden without changing cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real radix-32 divider's one-hot candidate masking and
balanced OR reduction with a balanced tree of ordinary two-input muxes.
Preserve all 31 independent unsigned 38-bit subtractions, their full
borrow bits, registered 37-bit multiples, and the exact radix and
request/preparation/iteration/completion schedule. Do not change any
ordinary ALU operation, multiplier, pipeline stage, or external port.

Let T be the existing 37-bit digit_trial and g[k]=!difference[k][37]
for k=1..31. For positive D these decisions form a thermometer code:
g[k] is true exactly when k <= floor(T/D). Because the legal recurrence
maintains R<D, T<32D and the winning digit is in 0..31. Construct
unmasked 37-bit leaves C[0]={T[31:0],5'd0} and
C[k]={difference[k][31:0],k[4:0]} for k=1..31. Remainder candidates
may be truncated only after retaining the original full-width borrow
decision; the selected nonnegative remainder fits 32 bits.

Build the following statically generated mux levels, with all indices
elaboration-time constants. A true decision always selects the upper
candidate or subtree:
  L1[j] = g[2*j+1]  ? C[2*j+1]  : C[2*j],  j=0..15;
  L2[j] = g[4*j+2]  ? L1[2*j+1] : L1[2*j], j=0..7;
  L3[j] = g[8*j+4]  ? L2[2*j+1] : L2[2*j], j=0..3;
  L4[j] = g[16*j+8] ? L3[2*j+1] : L3[2*j], j=0..1;
  selected_digit = g[16] ? L4[1] : L4[0].
Each node asks whether the winning digit reaches the lower boundary
of its upper half. Thus every path chooses exactly the same largest
successful subtraction as the current one-hot network. The select
decisions already exist independently: do not introduce a serial
priority encoder, a new subtract-after-selection stage, or a global
binary digit decoder feeding a variable-index array. Keep quotient
digit and remainder together in the same payload. No keep/preserve
attributes or added state are needed. Existing intermediate names
masked_digit and digit_or16/8/4/2 may be retained while changing their
assignments to the above unmasked leaves and mux levels; document
their new role. Remove the now-unused digit_select one-hot vector.

Preserve t0 magnitude capture, t1 widened-multiple/two-bit-prefix
preparation, six five-bit recurrence edges t2..t7, sticky completion,
and earliest result acceptance at t8. Preserve operand isolation,

Leave RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and controller timing untouched.
