title: Separate address generation and register complete memory requests
motivation:
The champion delivers 208.94 iterations/s at 83.245 MHz with 3984075
timed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path starts at ID/EX.pc[24]
and reaches data memory through EX/ALU result selection. The shared
alu_result currently carries arithmetic, AUIPC, jump links and division
results as well as memory addresses, while MEM formats store data and
derives byte masks and alignment. Prior structural successes isolated
operand and M-unit register boundaries; r10s1's control predecode did
not remove arithmetic paths. Split address generation from ordinary
register arithmetic and terminate memory-request preparation at EX/MEM.

title: Predecode PC-only training destinations for local predictor updates
motivation:
The champion already predicts direct branches and JAL and buffers four
fetches. Prior profiling reported only 55124 direction misses among
529588 conditional branches, so adding prediction capacity has limited
throughput headroom. The current training circuit reads an indexed
two-bit counter, computes its saturated successor, and writes through
variable bitplane indices directly from EX resolution. Removing that
shared read/modify/write network is a predictor timing opportunity.
Prior comparator/predecode changes r9s2-r11s2 lost Fmax; r9s2 also
reports unsuccessful distributed-counter probes on an older champion.
This proposal specifically registers the training destination before
resolution and retains the original prediction policy and update cycle.

title: Use threshold mux selection in the memory-request champion's divider
motivation:
The current champion separates complete memory requests at EX/MEM but
retains the radix-32 divider's one-hot candidate masking and OR tree.
The prior micro_opt experiment hyp-20261002-001-r12s0 replaced that
selection network with threshold-controlled muxes and reached 89.392
MHz versus its 83.245 MHz parent, using 122 fewer LUTs with unchanged
CoreMark cycles. It lost the tournament to the separate memory-request
change, rather than failing correctness. Apply that local selection
optimization to the new champion, whose median Fmax is 89.575 MHz and
fitness is 224.83. This is evidence for the mechanism, not proof that
the gains compose: branch recovery and EX forwarding remain competing
paths. Avoid earlier unsuccessful carry-select and ALU-decode rewrites.

title: Register direct control-transfer targets before execute
motivation: The champion reaches 224.83 iterations/s at 89.575 MHz with 3984075 measured CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst placement-0 path crosses EX branch resolution and fetch, while nearby paths include PC-derived values feeding EX selection and ID forwarding. Successful structural changes have moved complete operands and memory requests across existing registers. Predictor outcome predecode and local arithmetic rewrites repeatedly failed. Preserve raw PC, immediate and RVFI operands, branch comparisons, trap-adjusted write eligibility and alignment-fault behavior. A taken misaligned direct transfer still traps with the existing sequential pc_next fallback and suppresses link writes as before; a not-taken misaligned branch target does not trap. Keep control_advance, redirect qualification, train_valid/index/agree and saved predicted_taken unchanged. No direction or prediction outcome is calculated in ID. Correct prediction, recovery, FENCE.I serialization, early JAL, ordinary JALR, queue conservation and empty bypass have their exact current latency and behavior.

Keep memory-request generation, load/MUL interlocks, youngest-writer forwarding, sticky divider completion, the t8 divide handshake and both real and ALTOPS arithmetic unchanged. Preserve nret=1, all top-level ports, default-illegal decoding, exact-once memory effects, architectural retirement order and every hard invariant. Contract files, firmware and evaluator configuration remain untouched.

The intended gain is removing the direct PC-plus-immediate adder from the EX target/alignment network before recovery and trap qualification. Its new ID inputs are independent of the already-long operand-forwarding path. The cost is 32 payload bits and an ID adder; synthesis may share or prune existing arithmetic. Remaining divider recurrence and ordinary ALU-to-ID feedback limit the headroom.

Replace the single fetch PC register with two 32-bit candidate-address registers and one registered recovery selector. Keep all address bits; do not narrow or mask addresses. normal_pc_q holds the normal predictor-selected successor; recovery_pc_q holds the EX correction address. The active PC is recovering_q ? recovery_pc_q : normal_pc_q, and must drive every existing PC use: imem_addr, raw_fetch.pc, agree-table indexing, direct-target generation and PC+4. Capture normal_pc_q only on the existing fetch_accept, independently of redirect. Capture recovery_pc_q only on redirect; otherwise retain it. This removes the inactive-bank speculative writes and the selector-dependent update-enable term. Set recovering_q on redirect, otherwise clear it on fetch_accept, otherwise hold it. Reset both address banks to RESET_PC and recovering_q to zero. Every transition that selects the recovery bank must capture the new redirect_target on that same edge.

On a redirect edge, the freshly captured correction bank becomes active and the existing FIFO flush discards every younger entry. During an instruction-bus hold after recovery, recovering_q remains set and the correction bank holds its address. On the first subsequent fetch_accept, normal_pc_q captures next_pc computed from the active correction address while the selector clears. A redirect concurrent with fetch_accept overrides the selector and captures a new correction address; any simultaneous normal-bank write is harmless. Consecutive redirects, repeated resets, queue-full holds and simultaneous predictor training must reproduce the original external PC recurrence exactly: reset ? RESET_PC : redirect ? redirect_target : fetch_accept ? next_pc : old_pc.

title: Move decode stall to the final fetch-queue payload selection
motivation:
The champion reaches 224.83 iterations/s at 89.575 MHz. Prior micro_opt
attempts at carry select, registered ALU decode, divider selection and
the final EX result mux did not produce an accepted gain on this parent.
The r14s0 timing report exposes an IF count_q-to-queue-payload path
through hazard/ID logic. The fixed-head FIFO computes count_q - pop
and decodes that index after the late consumer-stall decision. It also
qualifies all shifts with nonempty occupancy even though empty payload
contents are unobservable. Factor stall out of this control network.

attempts at carry select, registered ALU decode, divider selection and

and decodes that index after the late consumer-stall decision. It also

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only the next-data equations of the existing four fixed-head
instruction FIFO payload registers. Keep binary count_q, its transition
logic, fetch_accept, push and pop exactly unchanged. Remove push_index
and the priority write/shift/hold chain. For entries i=0..3 prepare
held_data_i = (fetch_accept && count_q == i) ? raw_fetch : queue_q[i].
For entries i=0..2 also prepare
advanced_data_i = (fetch_accept && count_q == i+1)
                  ? raw_fetch : queue_q[i+1].
Set advanced_data_3 = queue_q[3]. Clock every payload entry with
queue_q[i] <= stall ? held_data_i : advanced_data_i.
Use static generate-time indices and width-correct three-bit count
comparisons, ordinary ternary muxes, and no preservation attributes.

The held and advancing payload candidates depend on registered count
and raw readiness, not consumer stall. Stall controls only the final
two-input data selection. Removing the pop-dependent index arithmetic
and redundant nonempty qualification moves work before that late mux.
Keep syn_ramstyle="registers", the fixed decode head, raw-response
fall-through, the full bundle layout and the existing output mux.

Empty, unstalled cycles may shift invalid payload bits; occupancy stays
zero and output continues to bypass raw_fetch. This is intentional and
cannot expose an instruction: refill overwrites each newly valid slot,
and shifting preserves the valid prefix. Nonempty queue contents and
all visible behavior must match the original cycle by cycle. Full
queues still accept no raw fetch during a pop, so tail entry 3 holds
when advancing. Occupancies 1..3 permit simultaneous head consumption
and tail insertion. When held, raw data appends at the old occupancy.
Reset/redirect clear occupancy with original priority; payload writes
remain independent of both signals, and flushed contents remain inert.

This is one local control/data-mux micro-optimization. Preserve queue
capacity, occupancy state, predictor and training, PC advancement and
recovery, FENCE.I, backend and bus stalls, instruction latency, hazard
equations, all execution arithmetic and forwarding. Keep nret=1, ports,

title: Use a dedicated decode head with a two-slot circular fetch tail
motivation: The four-entry shift FIFO hides fetch stalls, but vendor paths cross its occupancy, hazard and insertion-control loop. A registered decode head with a circular tail preserves the short decode read path. Four-entry prototypes measured 88.650 MHz with binary tail pointers and 88.842 MHz with one-hot occupancy, below the 89.575 MHz champion. The proposed three-entry structure instead uses a two-slot tail: one-bit pointers, a two-way head-refill mux and one fewer full instruction bundle. This targets queue control and routing cost while retaining empty bypass and fetch/backend overlap.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure instruction buffering as one dedicated decode-head register and two circular tail registers, for total capacity three. This is a single structural fetch-queue hypothesis. Preserve single issue, nret=1, the predictor, raw empty bypass and the existing execution pipeline. The selected tail data feeds only the head register at an edge; decode sees the registered head or the existing raw empty bypass, never a pointer-selected tail read.

Retain count_q with its current three-bit width so existing observations remain available, but restrict occupancy to 0..3. Define fetch_accept = imem_ready && count_q != 3; pop = count_q != 0 && !stall; push = fetch_accept && (count_q != 0 || stall). Update count by +1 on push only, -1 on pop only, and hold on both/neither. A full queue rejects the raw response even on a simultaneous pop and resumes fetching next cycle, keeping capacity independent of combinational decode-ready. Advance the fetch PC only on fetch_accept, with the existing reset/redirect priority and predictor.

Store complete if_id_t bundles in one head_q and two flop-backed tail_q entries. On push into an empty queue, capture raw_fetch into head_q. On pop with old count greater than one, refill head_q from tail_q[tail_read_q]. On pop with old count equal to one and fetch_accept, replace the head directly with raw_fetch. Otherwise retain the head payload. A consumed raw empty bypass is not enqueued.

Use one-bit tail_read_q and tail_write_q pointers. Define tail_pop = pop && count_q > 1 and tail_push = push && (count_q > 1 || (count_q == 1 && !pop)). Write raw_fetch into the selected tail slot only on tail_push. Toggle each pointer only on its corresponding tail transfer. Reset and redirect clear count and both pointers. No modulo-three arithmetic or three-way read mux remains. Old-state reads on simultaneous tail transfers preserve FIFO order. At count one, simultaneous pop/push replaces only the head and moves neither pointer. At count three, raw acceptance is inhibited, so a full-tail pop cannot collide with a same-slot push.

Remove the shifting queue entries, count-minus-pop insertion arithmetic and shift/append arbitration. Force flop storage as in the existing queue. Payload writes need no recovery/reset gating: occupancy and reset pointers invalidate flushed entries. Keep each saved instruction, PC, valid and predicted_taken together. Preserve recovery during imem stalls, deferred EX recovery during older dmem holds, predictor training cadence and FENCE.I flushing.

Change no ALU, forwarding, divider, multiplier, memory handshake or retirement behavior. Preserve nret=1, top-level ports, decoder legality, traps, all hard invariants and all protected files. Do not combine this proposal with AUIPC retiming or arithmetic changes.

The tradeoff is a smaller queue, which can increase fetch-empty cycles, in exchange for simpler control, less movement and lower storage/routing cost. Unlike the four-entry probes, the tail has power-of-two depth and only a two-way refill mux. Predict a six-percent fitness improvement with low confidence; the final three-entry proposal has no completed vendor timing measurement and has not demonstrated acceptance. Judge actual median Fmax times measured iterations/cycle, including the smaller queue's cycle cost. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 235.17218 iterations/s.

Run lint, an adapted independent FIFO conservation model, existing architectural pipeline checks, full RVFI cosimulation under ready/stalled buses, the unchanged formal gate, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks and all three Gowin placements. Update only occupancy/capacity-dependent timing expectations to capacity three; preserve all exact-once, ordering, operand, trap and bounded-progress assertions. Formal proof remains required.

title: Predict fetch successors from a tagged direct-target cache
motivation:
The existing predictor computes a B/J immediate and a full-width target
from the current instruction response before choosing the next fetch PC.
Prediction therefore feeds instruction-memory output back into its own
address path. Earlier agree prediction improved throughput, but recent
recovery-mux and PC-bank changes gained only 0.31 percent or regressed.
Direction accuracy alone has limited headroom: a prior architectural
profile recorded roughly 55124 conditional misses in about four million
timed cycles. Change where predicted targets come from, rather than
pursuing another small recovery-mux rewrite or merely enlarging the BHT.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace raw-instruction direct-target prediction with a 32-entry,
direct-mapped tagged branch-target cache indexed by fetch PC[6:2]. Each
entry holds valid, the full remaining PC tag [31:7], an aligned 30-bit
target [31:2], conditional-versus-JAL kind, and the branch-immediate sign
bias. Use asynchronous flop-based lookup, with explicit fixed-entry
writes and banked/balanced selection suitable for Gowin. Reset only valid
bits; invalid payloads must never select a target. Do not truncate tags
or architectural addresses to the benchmark memory size.

Keep the existing sixteen two-bit agree counters and their PC[5:2]
index, weakly-agree initialization, current-state saturation and
pre-edge read/write semantics. On a matching cache entry predict JAL
taken, or predict a conditional branch taken when its stored bias
agrees with the selected counter MSB. Select the cached target directly.
On a miss or predicted-not-taken hit select PC+4. No raw-instruction
decode or B/J target adder may feed the normal next-fetch-PC selection,
including on misses; adding the old combinational fallback would retain
the path this hypothesis is intended to remove. JALR stays unpredicted.
The first execution of an uncached direct transfer pays ordinary EX
recovery, and repeated hits reuse the registered target.

Fill or refresh an entry exactly once when a valid, legal, aligned direct
branch or JAL advances from EX. Conditional branches may allocate even
when not taken; store their actual PC-relative target, never PC+4 from a
not-taken retirement. Leave agree-counter training eligibility unchanged.
A held, annulled, illegal or misaligned control transfer must not allocate.
Invalidate a matching stale entry when its PC resolves as a non-direct
instruction or an uncacheable direct instruction. Invalidate all cache
valid bits on reset and advancing FENCE.I, with priority over allocation.
FENCE.I retains the existing queue flush, memory ordering and PC+4 restart.
Ordinary recovery need not clear correct entries. Training uses resolved
instruction PCs and targets, never the younger raw-fetch address.

Save the exact predicted successor with every fetch response in if_id_t,
every FIFO entry and id_ex_t. The saved value must be the pre-edge lookup
actually used to advance that fetch, including simultaneous same-index
training. Carry it through empty bypass, shifts, push/pop and all holds.
Check the complete saved successor against the actual successor on each
valid EX advancement, including non-control and illegal instructions;
a stale prediction at a PC whose instruction changed must still recover.
Derive the actual successor from existing branch/jump conditions, full
targets and misalignment fallback to PC+4. A wrong target is a mismatch
even when both predicted and actual directions are taken. Redirect to
the actual successor, not the old direction-only correction mux. Exclude
execute_wait and older dmem holds so each instruction recovers at most
once. FENCE.I remains an unconditional serialization redirect.

Retain the four-entry fixed-head queue, empty bypass, acceptance and
occupancy rules. Recovery still overrides unavailable imem and full
queues and annuls every younger instruction. Do not let mismatch feed
raw instruction data, register-file addresses, forwarding selection or
ID/EX payload enables. Architectural EX/MEM.pc_next and RVFI always use
the resolved successor; jump links, traps and memory side effects keep
their original rules. Preserve nret=1, every top-level port, all decoder
and retirement invariants, and both real and ALTOPS M-extension logic.

The intended gain is higher Fmax from removing instruction-response
decode and target arithmetic from speculative PC generation. This is
one target-source architecture change, with no added pipeline stage,
RAS, global history, direction-policy change or unrelated datapath edit.
Predict six percent higher fitness with low confidence. This candidate
has not been implemented or timed. Cache conflicts and cold misses can
increase cycles; tag/target muxes, EX successor equality, extra metadata
and placement pressure can outweigh the removed path. Existing EX-to-ID
and divider paths remain competing limits. Do not assume the champion's
3984075 timed cycles survive this policy change.

A reference-ISS profile of the canonical program between its MMIO markers
counted 2922016 instructions, 529588 conditional branches, 49367 JALs,
13735 JALRs and 223 distinct direct-control PCs. A retire-order model
with immediate training counted 55134 direct-transfer prediction errors
for the current agree policy, versus 75053 with the proposed 32-entry
cache: 19919 additional errors. The cache had 500895 hits and 78060
misses across 578955 direct transfers. Doubling to 64 entries reduced
errors by only 6756 while doubling target/tag storage, so keep this
hypothesis at 32 entries. This model omits pipeline-delayed training,
wrong-path fetches, queue state and bus stalls; it does not measure RTL
cycles, CRC correctness, Fmax or fitness. Use these numbers to justify
the capacity choice, not as a claimed performance improvement.

Validate cache hits, misses, full-tag aliases, target replacement,
same-cycle lookup/training, stale instruction kinds/targets, reset and
FENCE.I. Cover all legal branch functions and misaligned targets, held
branches, adjacent controls, non-control false hits, JALR fallback and
wrong-path stores under both bus stalls. Keep every architectural,
queue-conservation, RVFI and progress assertion; replace only test
assumptions specific to immediate cold JAL prediction with explicit
cold-miss and warmed-hit expectations. Run unchanged formal and RVFI
cosimulation gates, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation,
and all three Gowin placements. Measure cache-miss recovery cost and
marker cycles separately from Fmax. Acceptance requires measured median
Fmax times iterations/cycle strictly above 235.17218 iterations/second,
which is 224.83 times 1.046; no timing or accuracy improvement alone
establishes acceptance.
